   154→  const onActionResizeStart = useCallback(({ action }: { action: TimelineAction; row: TimelineRow; dir: string }) => {
   155→    const m = metaRef.current[action.id]
   156→    if (!m) return
   157→    resizeStartRef.current[action.id] = { start: action.start, end: action.end, from: m.from }
   158→  }, [])
   159→
   160→  const onActionResizeEnd = useCallback(({ action, row, dir }: { action: TimelineAction; row: TimelineRow; dir: string; start: number; end: number }) => {
   161→    if (dir === 'left') {
   162→      const orig = resizeStartRef.current[action.id]
   163→      if (orig) {
   164→        setMeta(prev => {
   165→          const m = prev[action.id]
   166→          if (!m) return prev
   167→          const startDelta = action.start - orig.start
   168→          return {
   169→            ...prev,
   170→            [action.id]: { ...m, from: Math.max(0, orig.from + startDelta * m.speed) },
   171→          }
   172→        })
   173→      }
   174→    } else if (dir === 'right') {
   175→      // Update meta.to to match the new action.end
   176→      setMeta(prev => {
   177→        const m = prev[action.id]
   178→        if (!m) return prev
   179→        const newTo = getSourceTime({ from: m.from, start: action.start, speed: m.speed }, action.end)
   180→        return {
   181→          ...prev,
   182→          [action.id]: { ...m, to: newTo },
   183→        }
   184→      })
   185→    }
   186→
   187→    // Ensure rows state reflects the final resize position and trigger save
   188→    setRows(prevRows => {
   189→      const updated = prevRows.map(r => {
   190→        if (r.id !== row.id) return r
   191→        return {
   192→          ...r,
   193→          actions: r.actions.map(a =>
   194→            a.id === action.id ? { ...a, start: action.start, end: action.end } : a
   195→          ),
   196→        }
   197→      })
   198→      scheduleSave(updated)
   199→      return updated
   200→    })
   201→
   202→    delete resizeStartRef.current[action.id]
   203→  }, [scheduleSave])
   204→
   205→  // Handle data changes from drag/resize
   206→  const onChange = useCallback((newRows: TimelineRow[]) => {
   207→    if (ignoreNextOnChange.current) return
   208→    setRows(newRows)
   209→    scheduleSave(newRows)
   210→    // After React commits the new rows, force the preview to re-sync.
   211→    // queueMicrotask ensures LivePreview has rendered with the new data
   212→    // and its syncVideoRef/syncAudioRef point to the latest functions.
   213→    queueMicrotask(() => {
   214→      previewRef.current?.refresh()
   215→    })
   216→  }, [scheduleSave])
   217→
   218→  // Custom action renderer
   219→  const getActionRender = useCallback((action: TimelineAction, _row: TimelineRow) => {
   220→    const m = meta[action.id]
   221→    if (!m) return null
   222→    const color = getAssetColor(m.asset)
   223→    const srcEnd = getSourceTime({ from: m.from, start: action.start, speed: m.speed }, action.end)
   224→    return (
   225→      <div
   226→        className="clip-action"
   227→        style={{ backgroundColor: color }}
   228→      >
   229→        <span className="clip-label">{m.asset}</span>
   230→        <span className="clip-time">
   231→          src {m.from.toFixed(1)}s - {srcEnd.toFixed(1)}s
   232→        </span>
   233→      </div>
   234→    )
   235→  }, [meta])
   236→
   237→  // Keyboard: space to toggle play
   238→  useEffect(() => {
   239→    const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
   240→      if (e.code === 'Space' && e.target === document.body) {
   241→        e.preventDefault()
   242→        previewRef.current?.togglePlayPause()
   243→      }
   244→    }
   245→    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)
   246→    return () => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey)
   247→  }, [])
   248→
   249→  const startRender = useCallback(async () => {
   250→    if (renderStatus === 'rendering') return
   251→    setRenderStatus('rendering')
   252→    setRenderLog('')
   253→    try {
   254→      const res = await fetch('/api/render', { method: 'POST' })
   255→      const reader = res.body?.getReader()
   256→      if (!reader) { setRenderStatus('error'); return }
   257→      const decoder = new TextDecoder()
   258→      let buf = ''
   259→      while (true) {
   260→        const { done, value } = await reader.read()
   261→        if (done) break
   262→        buf += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })
   263→        // Parse SSE events
   264→        const lines = buf.split('\n')
   265→        buf = lines.pop() ?? ''
   266→        for (const line of lines) {
   267→          if (line.startsWith('event: done')) {
   268→            setRenderStatus('done')
   269→            setRenderDirty(false)
   270→          } else if (line.startsWith('event: error')) {
   271→            setRenderStatus('error')
   272→          } else if (line.startsWith('data: ')) {
   273→            setRenderLog(prev => prev + line.slice(6) + '\n')
   274→          }
   275→        }
   276→      }
   277→    } catch {
   278→      setRenderStatus('error')
   279→    }
   280→  }, [renderStatus])
   281→
   282→  const formatTime = (t: number) => {
   283→    const mins = Math.floor(t / 60)
   284→    const secs = Math.floor(t % 60)
   285→    const ms = Math.floor((t % 1) * 100)
   286→    return `${mins}:${secs.toString().padStart(2, '0')}.${ms.toString().padStart(2, '0')}`
   287→  }
   288→
   289→  const statusIndicator = {
   290→    saved: '●', saving: '◌', dirty: '○', error: '✕',
   291→  }[saveStatus]
   292→
   293→  const statusColor = {
   294→    saved: '#98c379', saving: '#e5c07b', dirty: '#e5c07b', error: '#e06c75',
   295→  }[saveStatus]
   296→
   297→  if (!data) {
   298→    return <div className="app" style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center' }}>Loading timeline...</div>
   299→  }
   300→
   301→  return (
   302→    <div className="app">
   303→      <div className="top-bar">
   304→        <h1>Timeline Viewer</h1>
   305→        <div className="top-bar-right">
   306→          <button
   307→            className={`render-btn${renderDirty ? ' render-dirty' : ''}${renderStatus === 'rendering' ? ' rendering' : ''}`}
   308→            onClick={startRender}
   309→            disabled={renderStatus === 'rendering'}
   310→            title={renderLog || undefined}
   311→          >
   312→            {renderStatus === 'rendering' ? 'Rendering...' : renderDirty ? 'Render' : 'Render'}
   313→          </button>
   314→          <span className="save-status" style={{ color: statusColor }}>
   315→            {statusIndicator} {saveStatus}
   316→          </span>
   317→          <span className="timecode">{formatTime(currentTime)}</span>
   318→        </div>
   319→      </div>
   320→
   321→      <div className="video-container">
   322→        <LivePreview
   323→          ref={previewRef}
   324→          rows={rows}
   325→          meta={meta}
   326→          assetPaths={data.assetMap}
   327→          transcript={transcript}
   328→          onTimeUpdate={onPreviewTimeUpdate}
   329→        />
   330→      </div>
   331→
   332→      <div className="timeline-container">
   333→        <div className="track-labels">
   334→          {rows.map((row) => (
   335→            <div key={row.id} className="track-label">
   336→              {ROW_LABELS[row.id] ?? row.id}
   337→            </div>
   338→          ))}
   339→        </div>
   340→        <div className="timeline-wrapper">
   341→          <Timeline
   342→            ref={timelineRef}
   343→            style={{ width: '100%', height: '100%' }}
   344→            editorData={rows}
   345→            effects={data.effects}
   346→            onChange={onChange}
   347→            scale={5}
   348→            scaleWidth={160}
   349→            scaleSplitCount={5}
   350→            startLeft={20}
   351→            rowHeight={40}
   352→            autoScroll={true}
   353→            dragLine={true}
   354→            getActionRender={getActionRender}
   355→            onCursorDrag={onCursorDrag}
   356→            onClickTimeArea={onClickTimeArea}
   357→            onActionResizeStart={onActionResizeStart}
   358→            onActionResizeEnd={onActionResizeEnd}
   359→          />
   360→        </div>
   361→      </div>
   362→    </div>
   363→  )
   364→}
   365→
   366→export default App
   367→

> AGENT

Here's what changed:

**App.tsx** now has one central `applyTimelineEdit(newRows, metaUpdates?)` function. Every edit path flows through it:
- `onChange` (drag/move) → `applyTimelineEdit(newRows)`
- `onActionResizeEnd` (left or right resize) → `applyTimelineEdit(newRows, { [id]: { from: ... } })` or `{ to: ... }`
- Poll still sets state directly (since it replaces everything from YAML)

`applyTimelineEdit` does three things atomically: `setRows` + `setMeta` + `scheduleSave` + `refresh()`. No more scattered state updates that can get out of sync.

> Nano Banana 2 is Google's new state-of-the-art fast image generation and editing model


## Overview

- **Endpoint**: `https://fal.run/fal-ai/nano-banana-2`
- **Model ID**: `fal-ai/nano-banana-2`
- **Category**: text-to-image
- **Kind**: inference


## Pricing

Your request will cost **$0.08** per image. For **$1.00**, you can run this model **12** times. 2K and 4K outputs will be charged at **1.5** times and **2** times the standard rate, respectively. 0.5K (512px) resolution outputs will be charged at **0.75** times the standard rate. If web search is used, an additional $0.015 will be charged. **Note: Pricing is subject to change.**

For more details, see [fal.ai pricing](https://fal.ai/pricing).

## API Information

This model can be used via our HTTP API or more conveniently via our client libraries.
See the input and output schema below, as well as the usage examples.


### Input Schema

The API accepts the following input parameters:


- **`prompt`** (`string`, _required_):
  The text prompt to generate an image from.
  - Examples: "An action shot of a black lab swimming in an inground suburban swimming pool. The camera is placed meticulously on the water line, dividing the image in half, revealing both the dogs head above water holding a tennis ball in it's mouth, and it's paws paddling underwater."

- **`num_images`** (`integer`, _optional_):
  The number of images to generate. Default value: `1`
  - Default: `1`
  - Range: `1` to `4`

- **`seed`** (`integer`, _optional_):
  The seed for the random number generator.

- **`aspect_ratio`** (`Enum`, _optional_):
  The aspect ratio of the generated image. Supports extreme ratios: 4:1, 1:4, 8:1, 1:8. Use "auto" to let the model decide based on the prompt. Default value: `auto`
  - Default: `"auto"`
  - Options: `"auto"`, `"21:9"`, `"16:9"`, `"3:2"`, `"4:3"`, `"5:4"`, `"1:1"`, `"4:5"`, `"3:4"`, `"2:3"`, `"9:16"`, `"4:1"`, `"1:4"`, `"8:1"`, `"1:8"`

- **`output_format`** (`OutputFormatEnum`, _optional_):
  The format of the generated image. Default value: `"png"`
  - Default: `"png"`
  - Options: `"jpeg"`, `"png"`, `"webp"`

- **`safety_tolerance`** (`SafetyToleranceEnum`, _optional_):
  The safety tolerance level for content moderation. 1 is the most strict (blocks most content), 6 is the least strict. Default value: `"4"`
  - Default: `"4"`
  - Options: `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, `"4"`, `"5"`, `"6"`

- **`sync_mode`** (`boolean`, _optional_):
  If `True`, the media will be returned as a data URI and the output data won't be available in the request history.
  - Default: `false`

- **`resolution`** (`ResolutionEnum`, _optional_):
  The resolution of the image to generate. Default value: `"1K"`
  - Default: `"1K"`
  - Options: `"0.5K"`, `"1K"`, `"2K"`, `"4K"`

- **`limit_generations`** (`boolean`, _optional_):
  Experimental parameter to limit the number of generations from each round of prompting to 1. Set to `True` to to disregard any instructions in the prompt regarding the number of images to generate and ignore any intermediate images generated by the model. This may affect generation quality. Default value: `true`
  - Default: `true`

- **`enable_web_search`** (`boolean`, _optional_):
  Enable web search for the image generation task. This will allow the model to use the latest information from the web to generate the image.
  - Default: `false`

- **`thinking_level`** (`Enum`, _optional_):
  When set, enables model thinking with the given level ('minimal' or 'high') and includes thoughts in the generation. Omit to disable.
  - Options: `"minimal"`, `"high"`



**Required Parameters Example**:

```json
{
  "prompt": "An action shot of a black lab swimming in an inground suburban swimming pool. The camera is placed meticulously on the water line, dividing the image in half, revealing both the dogs head above water holding a tennis ball in it's mouth, and it's paws paddling underwater."
}
```

**Full Example**:

  "prompt": "An action shot of a black lab swimming in an inground suburban swimming pool. The camera is placed meticulously on the water line, dividing the image in half, revealing both the dogs head above water holding a tennis ball in it's mouth, and it's paws paddling underwater.",
  "num_images": 1,
  "aspect_ratio": "auto",
  "output_format": "png",
  "safety_tolerance": "4",
  "resolution": "1K",
  "limit_generations": true
}
```


### Output Schema

The API returns the following output format:

- **`images`** (`list<ImageFile>`, _required_):
  The generated images.
  - Array of ImageFile
  - Examples: [{"file_name":"nano-banana-2-t2i-output.png","content_type":"image/png","url":"https://storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/example_outputs/nano-banana-2-t2i-output.png"}]

- **`description`** (`string`, _required_):
  The description of the generated images.

## Usage Examples

### cURL

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url https://fal.run/fal-ai/nano-banana-2 \
  --header "Authorization: Key $FAL_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
     "prompt": "An action shot of a black lab swimming in an inground suburban swimming pool. The camera is placed meticulously on the water line, dividing the image in half, revealing both the dogs head above water holding a tennis ball in it's mouth, and it's paws paddling underwater."
   }'
```

### Python

Ensure you have the Python client installed:

```bash
pip install fal-client
```

Then use the API client to make requests:

```python
import fal_client

def on_queue_update(update):
    if isinstance(update, fal_client.InProgress):
        for log in update.logs:
           print(log["message"])

result = fal_client.subscribe(
    "fal-ai/nano-banana-2",
    arguments={
        "prompt": "An action shot of a black lab swimming in an inground suburban swimming pool. The camera is placed meticulously on the water line, dividing the image in half, revealing both the dogs head above water holding a tennis ball in it's mouth, and it's paws paddling underwater."
    },
    with_logs=True,
    on_queue_update=on_queue_update,
)
print(result)
```

### JavaScript

Ensure you have the JavaScript client installed:

```bash
npm install --save @fal-ai/client
```

Then use the API client to make requests:

```javascript
import { fal } from "@fal-ai/client";

const result = await fal.subscribe("fal-ai/nano-banana-2", {
  input: {
    prompt: "An action shot of a black lab swimming in an inground suburban swimming pool. The camera is placed meticulously on the water line, dividing the image in half, revealing both the dogs head above water holding a tennis ball in it's mouth, and it's paws paddling underwater."
  },
  logs: true,
  onQueueUpdate: (update) => {
    if (update.status === "IN_PROGRESS") {
      update.logs.map((log) => log.message).forEach(console.log);
    }
  },
});
console.log(result.data);
console.log(result.requestId);
```

3. Auto-ingests it (creates asset profile with visual description)
4. Prints next steps showing how to add it to `timeline.yaml` with `hold` for duration

Options: `--name` (filename), `--aspect` (16:9, 1:1, etc.), `--resolution` (0.5K-4K), `--format` (png/jpeg/webp), `--num` (1-4 images), `--seed`, `--no-ingest`.

You'll need to add `FAL_KEY=...` to your `.env` file.

> Nano Banana 2 is Google's new state-of-the-art image generation and editing model



## Overview

- **Endpoint**: `https://fal.run/fal-ai/nano-banana-2/edit`
- **Model ID**: `fal-ai/nano-banana-2/edit`
- **Category**: image-to-image
- **Kind**: inference


## Pricing

Your request will cost **$0.08** per image. For **$1.00**, you can run this model **12** times. 2K and 4K outputs will be charged at **1.5** times and **2** times the standard rate, respectively. 0.5K (512px) resolution outputs will be charged at **0.75** times the standard rate. If web search is used, an additional $0.015 will be charged. **Note: Pricing is subject to change.**

For more details, see [fal.ai pricing](https://fal.ai/pricing).

## API Information

This model can be used via our HTTP API or more conveniently via our client libraries.
See the input and output schema below, as well as the usage examples.


### Input Schema

The API accepts the following input parameters:


- **`prompt`** (`string`, _required_):
  The prompt for image editing.
  - Examples: "make a photo of the man driving the car down the california coastline"

- **`num_images`** (`integer`, _optional_):
  The number of images to generate. Default value: `1`
  - Default: `1`
  - Range: `1` to `4`

- **`seed`** (`integer`, _optional_):
  The seed for the random number generator.

- **`aspect_ratio`** (`Enum`, _optional_):
  The aspect ratio of the generated image. Supports extreme ratios: 4:1, 1:4, 8:1, 1:8. Default value: `auto`
  - Default: `"auto"`
  - Options: `"auto"`, `"21:9"`, `"16:9"`, `"3:2"`, `"4:3"`, `"5:4"`, `"1:1"`, `"4:5"`, `"3:4"`, `"2:3"`, `"9:16"`, `"4:1"`, `"1:4"`, `"8:1"`, `"1:8"`

- **`output_format`** (`OutputFormatEnum`, _optional_):
  The format of the generated image. Default value: `"png"`
  - Default: `"png"`
  - Options: `"jpeg"`, `"png"`, `"webp"`

- **`safety_tolerance`** (`SafetyToleranceEnum`, _optional_):
  The safety tolerance level for content moderation. 1 is the most strict (blocks most content), 6 is the least strict. Default value: `"4"`
  - Default: `"4"`
  - Options: `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, `"4"`, `"5"`, `"6"`

- **`sync_mode`** (`boolean`, _optional_):
  If `True`, the media will be returned as a data URI and the output data won't be available in the request history.
  - Default: `false`

- **`image_urls`** (`list<string>`, _required_):
  The URLs of the images to use for image-to-image generation or image editing.
  - Array of string
  - Examples: ["https://storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/example_inputs/nano-banana-edit-input.png","https://storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/example_inputs/nano-banana-edit-input-2.png"]

- **`resolution`** (`ResolutionEnum`, _optional_):
  The resolution of the image to generate. Default value: `"1K"`
  - Default: `"1K"`
  - Options: `"0.5K"`, `"1K"`, `"2K"`, `"4K"`

- **`limit_generations`** (`boolean`, _optional_):
  Experimental parameter to limit the number of generations from each round of prompting to 1. Set to `True` to to disregard any instructions in the prompt regarding the number of images to generate and ignore any intermediate images generated by the model. This may affect generation quality. Default value: `true`
  - Default: `true`

- **`enable_web_search`** (`boolean`, _optional_):
  Enable web search for the image generation task. This will allow the model to use the latest information from the web to generate the image.
  - Default: `false`

- **`thinking_level`** (`Enum`, _optional_):
  When set, enables model thinking with the given level ('minimal' or 'high') and includes thoughts in the generation. Omit to disable.
  - Options: `"minimal"`, `"high"`



**Required Parameters Example**:

```json
{
  "prompt": "make a photo of the man driving the car down the california coastline",
  "image_urls": [
    "https://storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/example_inputs/nano-banana-edit-input.png",
    "https://storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/example_inputs/nano-banana-edit-input-2.png"
  ]
}
```

**Full Example**:

```json
{
  "prompt": "make a photo of the man driving the car down the california coastline",
  "num_images": 1,
  "aspect_ratio": "auto",
  "output_format": "png",
  "safety_tolerance": "4",
  "image_urls": [
    "https://storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/example_inputs/nano-banana-edit-input.png",
    "https://storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/example_inputs/nano-banana-edit-input-2.png"
  ],
  "resolution": "1K",
  "limit_generations": true
}
```


### Output Schema

The API returns the following output format:

- **`images`** (`list<ImageFile>`, _required_):
  The edited images.
  - Array of ImageFile
  - Examples: [{"file_name":"nano-banana-2-edit-output.png","content_type":"image/png","url":"https://storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/example_outputs/nano-banana-2-edit-output.png"}]

- **`description`** (`string`, _required_):
  The description of the generated images.



**Example Response**:

```json
{
  "images": [
    {
      "file_name": "nano-banana-2-edit-output.png",
      "content_type": "image/png",
      "url": "https://storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/example_outputs/nano-banana-2-edit-output.png"
    }
  ],
  "description": ""
}
```


## Usage Examples

### cURL

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url https://fal.run/fal-ai/nano-banana-2/edit \
  --header "Authorization: Key $FAL_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
     "prompt": "make a photo of the man driving the car down the california coastline",
     "image_urls": [
       "https://storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/example_inputs/nano-banana-edit-input.png",
       "https://storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/example_inputs/nano-banana-edit-input-2.png"
     ]
   }'
```

### Python

Ensure you have the Python client installed:

```bash
pip install fal-client
```

Then use the API client to make requests:

```python
import fal_client

def on_queue_update(update):
    if isinstance(update, fal_client.InProgress):
        for log in update.logs:
           print(log["message"])

result = fal_client.subscribe(
    "fal-ai/nano-banana-2/edit",
    arguments={
        "prompt": "make a photo of the man driving the car down the california coastline",
        "image_urls": ["https://storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/example_inputs/nano-banana-edit-input.png", "https://storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/example_inputs/nano-banana-edit-input-2.png"]
    },
    with_logs=True,
    on_queue_update=on_queue_update,
)
print(result)
```

### JavaScript

Ensure you have the JavaScript client installed:

```bash
npm install --save @fal-ai/client
```

Then use the API client to make requests:

```javascript
import { fal } from "@fal-ai/client";

const result = await fal.subscribe("fal-ai/nano-banana-2/edit", {
  input: {
    prompt: "make a photo of the man driving the car down the california coastline",
    image_urls: ["https://storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/example_inputs/nano-banana-edit-input.png", "https://storage.googleapis.com/falserverless/example_inputs/nano-banana-edit-input-2.png"]
  },
  logs: true,
  onQueueUpdate: (update) => {
    if (update.status === "IN_PROGRESS") {
      update.logs.map((log) => log.message).forEach(console.log);
    }
  },
});
console.log(result.data);
console.log(result.requestId);
```

300→def ingest_image(path: Path) -> dict:
   301→    from PIL import Image
   302→    img = Image.open(str(path))
   303→    width, height = img.size
   304→
   305→    print("  Describing image with Claude...")
   306→    desc = describe_image_with_openai(str(path))
   307→
   308→    return {
   309→        "id": path.stem.lower().replace(" ", "-").replace(".", "-"),
   310→        "file": str(path.relative_to(ROOT)),
   311→        "type": "image",
   312→        "dimensions": f"{width}x{height}",
   313→        "description": desc,
   314→    }
   315→
   316→
   317→# ── yaml serialization ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   318→
   319→def _to_native(obj):
   320→    """Recursively convert numpy/non-standard types to plain Python for YAML."""
   321→    if isinstance(obj, dict):
   322→        return {k: _to_native(v) for k, v in obj.items()}
   323→    if isinstance(obj, list):
   324→        return [_to_native(v) for v in obj]
   325→    # numpy scalars
   326→    try:
   327→        import numpy as np
   328→        if isinstance(obj, (np.integer,)):
   329→            return int(obj)
   330→        if isinstance(obj, (np.floating,)):
   331→            return float(obj)
   332→        if isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):
   333→            return obj.tolist()
   334→    except ImportError:
   335→        pass
   336→    return obj
   337→
   338→
   339→# ── main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   340→
   341→def ingest(file_path: str) -> Path:
   342→    path = Path(file_path)
   343→    if not path.is_absolute():
   344→        path = ROOT / path
   345→    path = path.resolve()
   346→
   347→    if not path.exists():
   348→        print(f"Error: file not found: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
   349→        sys.exit(1)

Now I have a thorough understanding of the entire system. Here is my detailed implementation plan.

---

## Implementation Plan: Overlay/Compositing Feature

### Architecture Summary

The current system has three main layers:
1. **Data layer**: `timeline.yaml` defines clips with `at`, `track` (video/audio), `asset`, `from`, `to`, `speed`
2. **Render layer**: `render.py` builds an ffmpeg `filter_complex` that concatenates video segments (with black gap fills) and audio segments (with silence fills), then maps `[vfinal]` and `[afinal]`
3. **Viewer layer**: A React app using `@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor` with a canvas-based `LivePreview` that draws video frames and transcript text. `timeline-data.ts` parses YAML into the editor's row/action model with two rows: `row-video` and `row-audio`.

---

### 1. Timeline YAML Schema for Overlays

Add a new track type `overlay` to the clips array. Each overlay clip needs position/size metadata that video and audio clips do not have:

```yaml
clips:
  # ... existing video/audio clips ...
  - at: 2.0
    track: overlay
    asset: example-image1
    from: 0
    to: 3.0        # duration the overlay is visible (or use 'hold: 3.0' for images)
    x: 100          # x position in output pixels (from left)
    y: 50           # y position in output pixels (from top)
    width: 320      # rendered width in output pixels
    height: 180     # rendered height in output pixels (or omit for aspect-ratio preserve)
    opacity: 1.0    # optional, default 1.0
```

Key design decisions:
- **Position coordinates are in output resolution pixels** (e.g., 1280x720 space). This is the simplest model -- the viewer can convert to/from canvas coordinates using the known output resolution, and ffmpeg overlay filter uses pixel coordinates natively.
- **`width`/`height` are both optional** -- if only `width` is given, height preserves aspect ratio (and vice versa). If both given, the image is scaled to that exact size.
- **`opacity` is optional** (defaults to 1.0). Maps directly to ffmpeg's `format=rgba,colorchannelmixer=aa=<opacity>` before the overlay filter.
- Multiple overlays can exist at the same time (they stack in clip order, later clips on top).

### 2. Render.py FFmpeg Changes

The current render pipeline builds a linear concat of video segments into `[vfinal]`, then maps it. Overlays need to be composited **on top** of `[vfinal]` using ffmpeg's `overlay` filter.

**Strategy**: After producing `[vfinal]` from the concat, chain overlay filters sequentially. Each overlay becomes:

```
[input_idx:v] scale=W:H, format=rgba, colorchannelmixer=aa=OPACITY [ovl_i_scaled];
[prev_video][ovl_i_scaled] overlay=x=X:y=Y:enable='between(t,START,END)' [ovl_i_out]
```

Implementation steps in `build_ffmpeg_command`:

a. **Collect overlay clips** alongside video/audio clips (add `overlay_clips` list filtered from `all_clips`).

b. **Register overlay assets as inputs** using the existing `get_input_idx` mechanism. Image assets already get `-loop 1` prepended.

c. **After building `[vfinal]`**, iterate through overlay clips sorted by `at` time:
   - For each overlay, create a scale filter for the overlay image/video to the specified `width`x`height`.
   - If the overlay source is a video (not an image), apply `trim` for the `from`/`to` range.
   - If `opacity < 1.0`, add `format=rgba,colorchannelmixer=aa={opacity}`.
   - Apply `overlay=x={x}:y={y}:enable='between(t,{at},{at+duration})'` on top of the current video label.
   - Chain the output as the new "current" video label.

d. **The final label after all overlays** replaces `vfinal` in the `-map` output.

e. For the `enable` expression: `at` is the timeline position, and `at + clip_timeline_duration(clip)` is the end. The `between(t,...)` function in ffmpeg operates on the output timeline PTS which aligns with the concat output.

**Important edge case**: The `enable` parameter on the overlay filter is critical -- it means the overlay input is only composited during its time range. Without it, the overlay would appear for the entire video. Using `enable` avoids needing to restructure the concat pipeline.

### 3. Viewer: Timeline Data Parsing (`timeline-data.ts`)

a. **Extend `RawClip`** to include overlay fields:
   ```
   track: 'video' | 'audio' | 'overlay'
   x?: number
   y?: number
   width?: number
   height?: number
   opacity?: number
   ```

b. **Extend `ClipMeta`** with the same overlay fields.

c. **Add a third row** in `buildFromRaw`: `{ id: 'row-overlay', actions: overlayActions }`.

d. **Update `toYaml`** to serialize overlay clips back, including the `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `opacity` fields. Add `'row-overlay': 'overlay'` to `trackOrder`.

e. **Update `ROW_LABELS`** in `App.tsx` to include `'row-overlay': 'Overlay'`.

### 4. Viewer: LivePreview Overlay Rendering

The preview currently draws video frames to a canvas. Overlays need to be drawn **on top** after the video frame.

a. **Preload overlay image assets**: In the existing `useEffect` that creates `<video>` and `<audio>` elements, also create `<img>` elements for overlay image assets and store them in a new ref (`overlayImages`). For video overlays, reuse the video element pool.

b. **New `drawOverlays(time)` function**: After `drawVideoFrame` (or `drawTranscript`) completes:
   - Find all overlay clips active at the current time (`clips.filter(c => c.track === 'overlay' && time >= c.start && time < c.end)`).
   - For each, compute the canvas-space position by mapping from output resolution (1280x720) to actual canvas display size. The canvas is 1280x720 logical pixels but is CSS-scaled with letterboxing. Since the canvas logical size matches output resolution, the overlay `x`/`y`/`width`/`height` map directly to `ctx.drawImage(img, x, y, width, height)`.
   - Apply opacity via `ctx.globalAlpha = overlay.opacity` before drawing, then restore.
   - Draw overlays in clip order (later clips on top).

c. **Integrate into render loop**: Modify `syncVideo` to call `drawOverlays(time)` after drawing the video frame. Also call it after `drawTranscript` (overlays should appear even during gaps).

### 5. Viewer: Interactive Overlay Editing on Canvas

This is the most complex UI addition. The goal is drag-to-move and resize handles on the preview canvas.

a. **New component `OverlayEditor`**: A transparent div layered on top of the canvas (via absolute positioning in the `.live-preview` container). This avoids interfering with canvas drawing.

b. **Selection state**: Track which overlay clip is selected (click to select). Show a selection border with 8 resize handles (corners + edges).

c. **Coordinate mapping**: The canvas CSS size differs from its logical size (1280x720). Compute the scale factor and offset from the canvas element's `getBoundingClientRect()` vs its logical dimensions. All mouse events need to be transformed from screen space to output-resolution space.

d. **Drag behavior**:
   - `onMouseDown` on an overlay: start drag, record offset from overlay origin.
   - `onMouseMove`: update the overlay's `x`/`y` in meta, call `applyTimelineEdit` to propagate changes.
   - `onMouseUp`: finalize position.

e. **Resize behavior**:
   - `onMouseDown` on a resize handle: track which handle and the initial dimensions.
   - `onMouseMove`: compute new `width`/`height` (and possibly `x`/`y` for top/left handles). Optionally hold Shift for aspect-ratio lock.
   - `onMouseUp`: finalize.

f. **Integration with App.tsx**: 
   - Pass overlay clips, meta, and `applyTimelineEdit` callback to the `OverlayEditor`.
   - The `OverlayEditor` only shows overlays active at `currentTime`.
   - When an overlay is dragged/resized, it calls `applyTimelineEdit` with updated meta containing the new `x`/`y`/`width`/`height`.

g. **Visual indicators**: Draw semi-transparent overlay boundaries even when not selected, with a brighter border on hover. Selected overlay gets resize handles.

### 6. Changes to `view.py` (Text View Tool)

Update `compute_timeline_positions` and `render_view` to handle `track: overlay` clips. Display them as a separate section in the text output showing asset, position, size, and time range.

### 7. Implementation Sequence

1. **`timeline-data.ts`** -- Add overlay types and parsing (row, meta fields, serialization). Low risk, foundational.
2. **`timeline.yaml`** -- Add a sample overlay clip for testing.
3. **`App.tsx`** -- Add the overlay row label and pass overlay data through. Minor changes.
4. **`LivePreview.tsx`** -- Add overlay image preloading and `drawOverlays()` into the render loop. Medium complexity.
5. **`render.py`** -- Add overlay filter chain after `[vfinal]`. Medium complexity, testable with `--dry-run`.
6. **New `OverlayEditor.tsx`** -- Interactive drag/resize component. Highest complexity, can be done last since the feature works without interactive editing (you can set x/y/width/height in YAML manually).
7. **`App.css`** -- Styles for overlay selection, handles, and the overlay row.
8. **`view.py`** -- Minor update to display overlay clips in text view.

### 8. Potential Challenges

- **FFmpeg `enable` timing**: The `between(t,...)` expression operates on the output stream's PTS. After concat, PTS should be continuous from 0, but this needs verification. If not, `setpts=PTS-STARTPTS` on the concat output may be needed.
- **Multiple overlays at same time**: FFmpeg overlay filters must be chained sequentially (each takes the output of the previous). Order matters for z-stacking.
- **Canvas coordinate mapping for interactive editing**: The CSS-scaled canvas means mouse coordinates need careful transformation. The canvas is 1280x720 logical but may display at any CSS size with letterboxing.
- **Video overlays (not just images)**: If an overlay asset is a video, the preview needs to seek and play it similarly to the main video track. This adds significant complexity. Recommend starting with image-only overlays and adding video overlay support as a follow-up.
- **Performance**: Drawing multiple overlay images per frame in the RAF loop should be fine for a few overlays. The `drawImage` call on pre-loaded `<img>` elements is fast.

   257→def add_arguments(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser):

   264→def run(args: argparse.Namespace):
   265→    tl_path = Path(args.timeline)
   266→    if not tl_path.exists():
   267→        print(f"No timeline found at {tl_path}")
   268→        sys.exit(1)

   274→    elif args.preview:

   276→    else:
   277→        out_path = DEFAULT_OUTPUT
   278→
   279→    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

   281→    try:

   290→        return
   291→
   292→    print(f"Rendering → {out_path}")
   293→    print(f"Command: {' '.join(cmd[:6])}...")
   294→
   295→    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=False)
   296→    if result.returncode == 0:

    91→
    92→  for (const [i, clip] of timeline.clips.entries()) {
    93→    const speed = clip.speed ?? 1
    94→    const duration = (clip.to - clip.from) / speed
    95→    const action: TimelineAction = {
    96→      id: `clip-${i}`,
    97→      start: clip.at,
    98→      end: clip.at + duration,
    99→      effectId: `effect-${clip.asset}`,
   100→    }
   101→    meta[action.id] = {
   102→      asset: clip.asset,
   103→      track: clip.track,
   104→      from: clip.from,
   105→      to: clip.to,
   106→      speed,
   107→    }
   108→    if (clip.track === 'video') {
   109→      videoActions.push(action)
   110→    } else {
   111→      audioActions.push(action)
   112→    }
   113→  }
   114→
   115→  return {
   116→    rows: [
   117→      { id: 'row-video', actions: videoActions },
   118→      { id: 'row-audio', actions: audioActions },
   119→    ],
   120→    meta,
   121→    effects,
   122→    assetMap: timeline.asset_map,
   123→    header: { output: timeline.output, asset_map: timeline.asset_map },
   124→  }
   125→}
   126→
   127→// Parse yaml text into timeline data
   128→export function parseTimeline(text: string): TimelineData {
   129→  const timeline = yaml.load(text) as RawTimeline
   130→  return buildFromRaw(timeline)
   131→}
   132→
   133→// Convert editor state back to YAML string
   134→export function toYaml(
   135→  rows: TimelineRow[],
   136→  meta: Record<string, ClipMeta>,
   137→  header: TimelineData['header'],
   138→): string {
   139→  const clips: RawClip[] = []
   140→
   141→  const trackOrder: Record<string, 'video' | 'audio'> = {
   142→    'row-video': 'video',
   143→    'row-audio': 'audio',
   144→  }
   145→
   146→  for (const row of rows) {
   147→    const track = trackOrder[row.id]
   148→    if (!track) continue
   149→    const sorted = [...row.actions].sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start)
   150→    for (const action of sorted) {
   151→      const m = meta[action.id]
   152→      if (!m) continue
   153→
   154→      const clip: RawClip = {
   155→        at: round(action.start),
   156→        track,
   157→        asset: m.asset,
   158→        from: round(m.from),
   159→        to: round(getSourceTime({ from: m.from, start: action.start, speed: m.speed }, action.end)),
   160→      }
   161→      if (m.speed !== 1) {
   162→        clip.speed = round(m.speed)
   163→      }
   164→      clips.push(clip)
   165→    }
   166→  }
   167→
   168→  const doc = {
   169→    output: header.output,
   170→    asset_map: header.asset_map,
   171→    clips,
   172→  }
   173→
   174→  return yaml.dump(doc, {
   175→    lineWidth: -1,
   176→    noRefs: true,
   177→    quotingType: '"',
   178→    forceQuotes: false,
   179→  })
   180→}
   181→
   182→function round(n: number): number {
   183→  return Math.round(n * 100) / 100
   184→}
   185→

    62→      const res = await fetch('/api/save-timeline', {
    63→        method: 'POST',
    64→        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/yaml' },
    65→        body: yamlStr,
    66→      })
    67→      if (res.ok) {
    68→        setSaveStatus('saved')
    69→        setRenderDirty(true)
    70→      } else {
    71→        setSaveStatus('error')
    72→      }
    73→    } catch {
    74→      setSaveStatus('error')
    75→    }
    76→  }, [])
    77→
    78→  const scheduleSave = useCallback((currentRows: TimelineRow[]) => {

    84→  /**
    85→   * Central update function. All edits to rows/meta go through here.

    88→  const applyTimelineEdit = useCallback((
    89→    newRows: TimelineRow[],
    90→    metaUpdates?: Record<string, Partial<ClipMeta>>,

    92→    setRows(newRows)
    93→
    94→    if (metaUpdates && Object.keys(metaUpdates).length > 0) {
    95→      setMeta(prev => {
    96→        const next = { ...prev }
    97→        for (const [id, patch] of Object.entries(metaUpdates)) {
    98→          if (next[id]) {
    99→            next[id] = { ...next[id], ...patch }
   100→          }
   101→        }
   102→        return next
   103→      })
   104→    }
   105→
   106→    scheduleSave(newRows)
   107→    // Refresh preview after React commits the new state
   108→    queueMicrotask(() => previewRef.current?.refresh())
   109→  }, [scheduleSave])

   111→  // ── Poll for external yaml changes ────────────────────────────────────────
   112→
   113→  const lastYaml = useRef('')
   114→  useEffect(() => {

   116→      try {
   117→        const res = await fetch('/api/timeline')
   118→        const text = await res.text()

   123→          setData(d)
   124→          setRows(d.rows)

   127→          setRenderDirty(true)

   129→      } catch {}
   130→    }

   237→      >

   247→  useEffect(() => {
   248→    const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {

   250→        e.preventDefault()

   252→      }

   254→    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)

   258→  const startRender = useCallback(async () => {
   259→    if (renderStatus === 'rendering') return
   260→    setRenderStatus('rendering')
   261→    setRenderLog('')
   262→    try {
   263→      const res = await fetch('/api/render', { method: 'POST' })
   264→      const reader = res.body?.getReader()
   265→      if (!reader) { setRenderStatus('error'); return }
   266→      const decoder = new TextDecoder()
   267→      let buf = ''
   268→      while (true) {
   269→        const { done, value } = await reader.read()
   270→        if (done) break
   271→        buf += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })
   272→        const lines = buf.split('\n')
   273→        buf = lines.pop() ?? ''

   275→          if (line.startsWith('event: done')) {

   278→          } else if (line.startsWith('event: error')) {

   295→  }
   296→
   297→  const statusIndicator = {
   298→    saved: '●', saving: '◌', dirty: '○', error: '✕',
   299→  }[saveStatus]
   300→
   301→  const statusColor = {
   302→    saved: '#98c379', saving: '#e5c07b', dirty: '#e5c07b', error: '#e06c75',
   303→  }[saveStatus]
   304→
   305→  if (!data) {
   306→    return <div className="app" style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center' }}>Loading timeline...</div>
   307→  }
   308→
   309→  return (
   310→    <div className="app">
   311→      <div className="top-bar">
   312→        <h1>Timeline Viewer</h1>
   313→        <div className="top-bar-right">

   315→            className={`render-btn${renderDirty ? ' render-dirty' : ''}${renderStatus === 'rendering' ? ' rendering' : ''}`}
   316→            onClick={startRender}
   317→            disabled={renderStatus === 'rendering'}
   318→            title={renderLog || undefined}
   319→          >
   320→            {renderStatus === 'rendering' ? 'Rendering...' : renderDirty ? 'Render' : 'Render'}
   321→          </button>
   322→          <span className="save-status" style={{ color: statusColor }}>
   323→            {statusIndicator} {saveStatus}
   324→          </span>
   325→          <span className="timecode">{formatTime(currentTime)}</span>
   326→        </div>
   327→      </div>
   328→
   329→      <div className="video-container">

   340→      <div className="timeline-container">

   342→          {rows.map((row) => (

1→"""
     2→Shared utilities for all video editor tools.
     3→
     4→Importing this module auto-loads .env from the project root.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→import json
     8→import os
     9→import subprocess
    10→from pathlib import Path
    11→
    12→import yaml
    13→
    14→# ── paths ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    15→
    16→ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent
    17→PROFILES_DIR = ROOT / "asset_profiles"
    18→TIMELINE_FILE = ROOT / "timeline.yaml"
    19→
    20→# ── auto-load .env ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    21→
    22→_env_file = ROOT / ".env"
    23→if _env_file.exists():
    24→    for _line in _env_file.read_text().splitlines():
    25→        _line = _line.strip()
    26→        if _line and not _line.startswith("#") and "=" in _line:
    27→            _k, _v = _line.split("=", 1)
    28→            os.environ.setdefault(_k.strip(), _v.strip())
    29→
    30→# ── subprocess helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    31→
    32→
    33→def run_cmd(cmd: list[str], **kwargs) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    34→    return subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, **kwargs)
    35→
    36→
    37→def ffprobe_json(path: str) -> dict:
    38→    r = run_cmd(["ffprobe", "-v", "quiet", "-print_format", "json",
    39→                 "-show_format", "-show_streams", path])
    40→    return json.loads(r.stdout)
    41→
    42→
    43→def audio_duration(audio_path: str) -> float:
    44→    """Return duration of audio file in seconds via ffprobe."""
    45→    r = run_cmd(["ffprobe", "-v", "quiet", "-print_format", "json",
    46→                 "-show_format", audio_path])
    47→    return float(json.loads(r.stdout)["format"]["duration"])
    48→
    49→
    50→# ── profile helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    51→
    52→_profile_cache: dict[str, dict] = {}
    53→_profile_paths: dict[str, Path] = {}
    54→
    55→
    56→def load_profile(asset_id: str) -> dict | None:
    57→    if asset_id in _profile_cache:
    58→        return _profile_cache[asset_id]
    59→    for f in PROFILES_DIR.glob("*.yaml"):
    60→        p = yaml.safe_load(f.read_text())
    61→        if p.get("id") == asset_id:
    62→            _profile_cache[asset_id] = p
    63→            _profile_paths[asset_id] = f
    64→            return p
    65→    return None
    66→
    67→
    68→def get_profile_path(asset_id: str) -> Path | None:
    69→    if asset_id not in _profile_paths:
    70→        load_profile(asset_id)
    71→    return _profile_paths.get(asset_id)
    72→
    73→
    74→def load_all_profiles() -> list[dict]:
    75→    profiles = []
    76→    for f in PROFILES_DIR.glob("*.yaml"):
    77→        try:
    78→            p = yaml.safe_load(f.read_text())
    79→            profiles.append(p)
    80→        except Exception:
    81→            pass
    82→    return sorted(profiles, key=lambda p: p.get("file", ""))
    83→
    84→
    85→# ── yaml helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    86→
    87→
    88→def save_yaml(data, path: Path):
    89→    with open(path, "w") as f:
    90→        yaml.dump(data, f, allow_unicode=True, sort_keys=False, default_flow_style=False)
    91→
    92→
    93→# ── openai client ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    94→
    95→
    96→def get_openai_client():
    97→    import openai
    98→    api_key = os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY", "")
    99→    if not api_key:
   100→        return None
   101→    return openai.OpenAI(api_key=api_key)

    22→def _call_llm_summary(descriptions: list[str]) -> str:
    23→    client = get_openai_client()
    24→    if not client:
    25→        return descriptions[0] if descriptions else "(no description)"
    26→    bullets = "\n".join(f"- {d}" for d in descriptions)
    27→    response = client.chat.completions.create(
    28→        model="gpt-4o-mini",
    29→        max_tokens=80,
    30→        messages=[{"role": "user", "content":
    31→            "Summarise what's shown in this video clip in one concise sentence. "
    32→            "Focus on the main on-screen content (UI, action, subject). No fluff.\n\n"
    33→            f"Frame descriptions:\n{bullets}"
    34→        }],
    35→    )
    36→    return response.choices[0].message.content.strip()
    37→
    38→
    39→def get_visual_summary(asset_id: str, src_s: float, src_e: float) -> str:
    40→    """
    41→    Return a one-sentence visual summary for a source range. Priority:
    42→      1. Range-specific cache: visual_summaries["{src_s:.2f}-{src_e:.2f}"] in profile
    43→      2. Whole-asset summary:  visual_summary in profile (written by ingest)
    44→      3. Generate via API for this range, then cache it
    45→    """
    46→    profile = load_profile(asset_id)
    47→    if not profile:
    48→        return "(no profile)"
    49→
    50→    # 1. Range-specific cache
    51→    cache_key = f"{src_s:.2f}-{src_e:.2f}"
    52→    cached = profile.get("visual_summaries", {}).get(cache_key)
    53→    if cached:
    54→        return cached
    55→
    56→    # 2. Whole-asset summary from ingest
    57→    if profile.get("visual_summary"):
    58→        return profile["visual_summary"]
    59→
    60→    # 3. Generate for this range and cache
    61→    segs = visual_in_range(profile, src_s, src_e)
    62→    if not segs:
    63→        return "(no visual description)"
    64→
    65→    print(f"  [summarising {asset_id} {src_s:.1f}s–{src_e:.1f}s via API…]", file=sys.stderr)
    66→    summary = _call_llm_summary([s["description"] for s in segs])
    67→
    68→    if "visual_summaries" not in profile:
    69→        profile["visual_summaries"] = {}
    70→    profile["visual_summaries"][cache_key] = summary
    71→    path = get_profile_path(asset_id)

    80→def fmt_t(seconds: float) -> str:
    81→    m = int(seconds) // 60
    82→    s = seconds - m * 60
    83→    return f"{m:02d}:{s:06.3f}"

    86→# ── transcript helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    87→
    88→def transcript_in_range(profile: dict, start: float, end: float) -> str:
    89→    """Return the words spoken between start and end seconds in the asset."""
    90→    transcript = profile.get("transcript", {})
    91→    words = transcript.get("words", [])
    92→    if not words:
    93→        segments = transcript.get("segments", [])
    94→        parts = []
    95→        for seg in segments:
    96→            if seg["end"] <= start or seg["start"] >= end:
    97→                continue
    98→            parts.append(seg["text"])
    99→        return " ".join(parts).strip()
   100→
   101→    clipped = [w["word"] for w in words if w["start"] >= start and w["end"] <= end]
   102→    return " ".join(clipped).strip()
   103→
   104→
   105→def sentence_boundary_check(profile: dict, clip_start: float, clip_end: float) -> dict:
   106→    transcript = profile.get("transcript", {})
   107→    segments = transcript.get("segments", [])
   108→    silence = profile.get("silence_regions", [])
   109→
   110→    def in_silence(t: float) -> bool:
   111→        return any(r["start"] <= t <= r["end"] for r in silence)
   112→
   113→    def at_sentence_start(t: float) -> bool:
   114→        return any(abs(seg["start"] - t) < 0.15 for seg in segments)
   115→
   116→    def at_sentence_end(t: float) -> bool:
   117→        return any(abs(seg["end"] - t) < 0.15 for seg in segments)
   118→
   119→    def surrounding_sentence(t: float) -> str | None:
   120→        for seg in segments:
   121→            if seg["start"] <= t <= seg["end"]:
   122→                return seg["text"]
   123→        return None
   124→
   125→    return {
   126→        "start_clean":    in_silence(clip_start) or at_sentence_start(clip_start),
   127→        "end_clean":      in_silence(clip_end)   or at_sentence_end(clip_end),
   128→        "start_sentence": surrounding_sentence(clip_start),
   129→        "end_sentence":   surrounding_sentence(clip_end),
   130→    }
   131→
   132→
   133→# ── visual helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   134→
   135→def preroll_silence(profile: dict, src_s: float, src_e: float) -> dict | None:
   136→    """Return info about silence before the first word in this source range, if any."""
   137→    words = profile.get("transcript", {}).get("words", [])
   138→    in_range = [w for w in words if w["start"] >= src_s and w["start"] < src_e]
   139→    if not in_range:
   140→        return None
   141→    first = in_range[0]
   142→    gap = round(first["start"] - src_s, 3)
   143→    if gap > 0.05:
   144→        return {"gap": gap, "word": first["word"], "src_at": first["start"]}
   145→    return None
   146→
   147→
   148→def visual_in_range(profile: dict, start: float, end: float) -> list[dict]:
   149→    return [s for s in profile.get("visual_segments", [])
   150→            if not (s["end"] <= start or s["start"] >= end)]
   151→
   152→
   153→# ── timeline computation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   154→
   155→def compute_timeline_positions(timeline: dict) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]:
   156→    """
   157→    Returns (video_clips, audio_clips), each clip enriched with:
   158→      timeline_start, timeline_end, source_start, source_end
   159→    """
   160→    video_clips: list[dict] = []
   161→    audio_clips: list[dict] = []
   162→
   163→    for clip in timeline.get("clips", []):
   164→        c = dict(clip)
   165→        at = float(c["at"])
   166→        src_start = float(c.get("from", 0.0))
   167→        if "hold" in c:
   168→            src_end = src_start + float(c["hold"])
   169→            c["to"] = src_end
   170→        else:
   171→            src_end = float(c.get("to", src_start))
   172→        src_dur = src_end - src_start
   173→        speed = float(c.get("speed", 1.0))
   174→        tl_dur = src_dur / speed
   175→
   176→        c["timeline_start"] = round(at, 3)
   177→        c["timeline_end"]   = round(at + tl_dur, 3)
   178→        c["source_start"]   = src_start
   179→        c["source_end"]     = src_end
   180→        c["speed"]          = speed
   181→
   182→        if c.get("track") == "audio":
   183→            audio_clips.append(c)
   184→        else:
   185→            video_clips.append(c)
   186→
   187→    return (
   188→        sorted(video_clips, key=lambda c: c["timeline_start"]),
   189→        sorted(audio_clips, key=lambda c: c["timeline_start"]),
   190→    )
   191→
   192→
   193→# ── issues detection ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   194→
   195→def find_issues(video_clips: list[dict], audio_clips: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
   196→    issues = []
   197→
   198→    video_end = max((c["timeline_end"] for c in video_clips), default=0.0)
   199→    audio_end = max((c["timeline_end"] for c in audio_clips), default=0.0)
   200→
   201→    if abs(video_end - audio_end) > 0.5:
   202→        longer  = "audio" if audio_end > video_end else "video"
   203→        shorter = "video" if audio_end > video_end else "audio"
   204→        issues.append(
   205→            f"{longer} track is {abs(audio_end - video_end):.1f}s longer than {shorter} "
   206→            f"({audio_end:.1f}s audio vs {video_end:.1f}s video)"
   207→        )
   208→
   209→    # Gaps in video track
   210→    for i in range(1, len(video_clips)):
   211→        gap = video_clips[i]["timeline_start"] - video_clips[i - 1]["timeline_end"]
   212→        if gap > 0.05:
   213→            issues.append(
   214→                f"Video gap of {gap:.2f}s: {fmt_t(video_clips[i-1]['timeline_end'])} → "
   215→                f"{fmt_t(video_clips[i]['timeline_start'])} "
   216→                f"(black screen — assign a clip)"
   217→            )
   218→
   219→    # Cut quality
   220→    for clip in video_clips:
   221→        profile = load_profile(clip["asset"])
   222→        if not profile or "transcript" not in profile:
   223→            continue
   224→        check = sentence_boundary_check(profile, clip["source_start"], clip["source_end"])
   225→        if not check["start_clean"]:
   226→            issues.append(
   227→                f"Clip '{clip['asset']}' starts mid-sentence at src {clip['source_start']:.1f}s"
   228→            )
   229→        if not check["end_clean"]:
   230→            issues.append(
   231→                f"Clip '{clip['asset']}' ends mid-sentence at src {clip['source_end']:.1f}s"
   232→            )
   233→
   234→    return issues
   235→
   236→
   237→# ── main view rendering ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   238→
   239→def render_view(timeline: dict, at: float | None = None, summary: bool = False) -> str:
   240→    video_clips, audio_clips = compute_timeline_positions(timeline)
   241→
   242→    if not video_clips and not audio_clips:
   243→        return "Timeline is empty."
   244→
   245→    total_duration = max(
   246→        (c["timeline_end"] for c in video_clips + audio_clips), default=0.0
   247→    )
   248→    out_cfg = timeline.get("output", {})
   249→    resolution = out_cfg.get("resolution", "?")
   250→    fps = out_cfg.get("fps", "?")
   251→
   252→    lines = []
   253→    lines.append("═" * 70)
   254→    lines.append(f"VIDEO TIMELINE VIEW  |  Total: {total_duration:.2f}s  |  {resolution} @ {fps}fps")
   255→    lines.append("═" * 70)
   256→
   257→    if at is not None:
   258→        lines.append(f"\nSNAPSHOT @ {fmt_t(at)} ({at:.3f}s)")
   259→        lines.append("─" * 70)
   260→
   261→        active_v = [c for c in video_clips if c["timeline_start"] <= at < c["timeline_end"]]
   262→        active_a = [c for c in audio_clips if c["timeline_start"] <= at < c["timeline_end"]]
   263→
   264→        if active_v:
   265→            for clip in active_v:
   266→                src_t = clip["source_start"] + (at - clip["timeline_start"])
   267→                profile = load_profile(clip["asset"])
   268→                lines.append(f"  VIDEO  {clip['asset']}  src:{src_t:.2f}s")
   269→                if profile:
   270→                    for seg in visual_in_range(profile, src_t - 0.1, src_t + 0.1):
   271→                        lines.append(f"    Visual: \"{seg['description']}\"")
   272→        else:
   273→            lines.append("  VIDEO: (black)")
   274→
   275→        if active_a:
   276→            for clip in active_a:
   277→                src_t = clip["source_start"] + (at - clip["timeline_start"])
   278→                profile = load_profile(clip["asset"])
   279→                vol_str = f"  vol:{clip.get('volume', 1.0)}" if float(clip.get("volume", 1.0)) != 1.0 else ""
   280→                lines.append(f"  AUDIO  {clip['asset']}  src:{src_t:.2f}s{vol_str}")
   281→                if profile:
   282→                    word_range = transcript_in_range(profile, max(0, src_t - 2), src_t + 2)
   283→                    if word_range:
   284→                        lines.append(f"    Speaking: \"{word_range}\"")
   285→        else:
   286→            lines.append("  AUDIO: (silence)")
   287→
   288→        return "\n".join(lines)
   289→
   290→    # Full view: walk through time segments defined by clip boundaries
   291→    boundaries: set[float] = set()
   292→    for c in video_clips + audio_clips:
   293→        boundaries.add(c["timeline_start"])
   294→        boundaries.add(c["timeline_end"])
   295→    sorted_boundaries = sorted(boundaries)
   296→
   297→    for i in range(len(sorted_boundaries) - 1):
   298→        seg_start = sorted_boundaries[i]
   299→        seg_end   = sorted_boundaries[i + 1]
   300→        mid       = (seg_start + seg_end) / 2
   301→
   302→        def _clip_sort_key(c):
   303→            return (c["timeline_start"], -(c["timeline_end"] - c["timeline_start"]))
   304→
   305→        active_v = sorted([c for c in video_clips if c["timeline_start"] <= mid < c["timeline_end"]], key=_clip_sort_key)
   306→        active_a = sorted([c for c in audio_clips if c["timeline_start"] <= mid < c["timeline_end"]], key=_clip_sort_key)
   307→
   308→        if not active_v and not active_a:
   309→            continue
   310→
   311→        dur = seg_end - seg_start
   312→        lines.append(f"\n[{fmt_t(seg_start)} → {fmt_t(seg_end)}]  ({dur:.2f}s)")
   313→
   314→        # Video clips
   315→        for clip in active_v:
   316→            src_s = clip["source_start"] + (seg_start - clip["timeline_start"])
   317→            src_e = clip["source_start"] + (seg_end   - clip["timeline_start"])
   318→            profile = load_profile(clip["asset"])
   319→
   320→            speed_str = f"  [{clip['speed']:.2f}x]" if clip.get("speed", 1.0) != 1.0 else ""
   321→            lines.append(f"  VIDEO  {clip['asset']}  [src: {src_s:.2f}s → {src_e:.2f}s]{speed_str}")
   322→
   323→            if profile:
   324→                if summary:
   325→                    vis = get_visual_summary(clip["asset"], src_s, src_e)
   326→                    lines.append(f"    \"{vis}\"")
   327→                else:
   328→                    for seg in visual_in_range(profile, src_s, src_e):
   329→                        rel_t = seg["start"] - clip["source_start"] + clip["timeline_start"]
   330→                        lines.append(f"    {fmt_t(rel_t)}  \"{seg['description']}\"")
   331→
   332→                if profile.get("type") in ("video+audio",):
   333→                    spoken = transcript_in_range(profile, src_s, src_e)
   334→                    if spoken:
   335→                        lines.append(f"    (embedded audio) \"{_wrap(spoken, 60)}\"")
   336→
   337→        # Audio clips
   338→        for clip in active_a:
   339→            src_s = clip["source_start"] + (seg_start - clip["timeline_start"])
   340→            src_e = clip["source_start"] + (seg_end   - clip["timeline_start"])
   341→            profile = load_profile(clip["asset"])
   342→            vol_str = f"  vol:{clip.get('volume', 1.0)}" if float(clip.get("volume", 1.0)) != 1.0 else ""
   343→
   344→            lines.append(f"  AUDIO  {clip['asset']}  [src: {src_s:.2f}s → {src_e:.2f}s]{vol_str}")
   345→
   346→            if profile:
   347→                # Pre-roll silence only worth flagging if gap is noticeable (>0.5s)
   348→                pr = preroll_silence(profile, src_s, src_e)
   349→                if pr and pr["gap"] >= 0.5:
   350→                    lines.append(f"    ~ pre-roll silence: {pr['gap']:.2f}s  (first word '{pr['word']}' at src {pr['src_at']:.2f}s)")
   351→
   352→                spoken = transcript_in_range(profile, src_s, src_e)
   353→                if spoken:
   354→                    lines.append(f"    \"{_wrap(spoken, 64)}\"")
   355→
   356→                # Only show silence markers >1s and only when video is also present
   357→                # (short pauses are natural; silence without video isn't a cut decision)
   358→                if active_v:
   359→                    for r in profile.get("silence_regions", []):
   360→                        dur_r = r["end"] - r["start"]
   361→                        if dur_r >= 1.0 and r["start"] >= src_s and r["end"] <= src_e:
   362→                            tl_s = clip["timeline_start"] + (r["start"] - clip["source_start"])
   363→                            tl_e = clip["timeline_start"] + (r["end"]   - clip["source_start"])
   364→                            lines.append(f"    ~ silence {fmt_t(tl_s)} → {fmt_t(tl_e)}"
   365→                                         f"  ({dur_r:.2f}s)")
   366→
   367→        lines.append("─" * 70)
   368→
   369→    # Issues summary
   370→    issues = find_issues(video_clips, audio_clips)
   371→    lines.append("")
   372→    if issues:
   373→        lines.append("ISSUES:")
   374→        for iss in issues:
   375→            lines.append(f"  ⚠  {iss}")
   376→    else:
   377→        lines.append("ISSUES:  none")
   378→    lines.append("═" * 70)
   379→
   380→    return "\n".join(lines)
   381→
   382→
   383→def _wrap(text: str, width: int) -> str:
   384→    words = text.split()
   385→    lines, current, length = [], [], 0
   386→    for w in words:
   387→        if length + len(w) + 1 > width and current:
   388→            lines.append(" ".join(current))
   389→            current, length = [], 0
   390→        current.append(w)
   391→        length += len(w) + 1
   392→    if current:
   393→        lines.append(" ".join(current))
   394→    return "\n             ".join(lines)
   395→
   396→
   397→# ── standard interface ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   398→
   399→
   400→def add_arguments(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser):
   401→    parser.add_argument("--at", type=float, default=None,
   402→                        help="Show snapshot at this timestamp (seconds)")
   403→    parser.add_argument("--summary", "-s", action="store_true",
   404→                        help="Compact view: one summarised visual per clip (cached via API)")
   405→    parser.add_argument("--timeline", default=str(TIMELINE_FILE),
   406→                        help="Path to timeline.yaml")
   407→
   408→
   409→def run(args: argparse.Namespace):
   410→    tl_path = Path(args.timeline)
   411→    if not tl_path.exists():
   412→        print(f"No timeline found at {tl_path}. Create timeline.yaml first.")
   413→        sys.exit(1)
   414→
   415→    timeline = yaml.safe_load(tl_path.read_text())
   416→    print(render_view(timeline, at=args.at, summary=args.summary))
   417→
   418→
   419→def main():
   420→    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
   421→        description="Generate a human/agent-readable view of the current timeline."
   422→    )
   423→    add_arguments(parser)
   424→    args = parser.parse_args()
   425→    run(args)
   426→
   427→
   428→if __name__ == "__main__":
   429→    main()
   430→

---

## Implementation Plan: Overlay/Compositing Feature

### Architecture Summary

The current system has three main layers:
1. **Data layer**: `timeline.yaml` defines clips with `at`, `track` (video/audio), `asset`, `from`, `to`, `speed`
2. **Render layer**: `render.py` builds an ffmpeg `filter_complex` that concatenates video segments (with black gap fills) and audio segments (with silence fills), then maps `[vfinal]` and `[afinal]`
3. **Viewer layer**: A React app using `@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor` with a canvas-based `LivePreview` that draws video frames and transcript text. `timeline-data.ts` parses YAML into the editor's row/action model with two rows: `row-video` and `row-audio`.

---

### 1. Timeline YAML Schema for Overlays

Add a new track type `overlay` to the clips array. Each overlay clip needs position/size metadata that video and audio clips do not have:

```yaml
clips:
  # ... existing video/audio clips ...
  - at: 2.0
    track: overlay
    asset: example-image1
    from: 0
    to: 3.0        # duration the overlay is visible (or use 'hold: 3.0' for images)
    x: 100          # x position in output pixels (from left)
    y: 50           # y position in output pixels (from top)
    width: 320      # rendered width in output pixels
    height: 180     # rendered height in output pixels (or omit for aspect-ratio preserve)
    opacity: 1.0    # optional, default 1.0
```

Key design decisions:
- **Position coordinates are in output resolution pixels** (e.g., 1280x720 space). This is the simplest model -- the viewer can convert to/from canvas coordinates using the known output resolution, and ffmpeg overlay filter uses pixel coordinates natively.
- **`width`/`height` are both optional** -- if only `width` is given, height preserves aspect ratio (and vice versa). If both given, the image is scaled to that exact size.
- **`opacity` is optional** (defaults to 1.0). Maps directly to ffmpeg's `format=rgba,colorchannelmixer=aa=<opacity>` before the overlay filter.
- Multiple overlays can exist at the same time (they stack in clip order, later clips on top).

### 2. Render.py FFmpeg Changes

The current render pipeline builds a linear concat of video segments into `[vfinal]`, then maps it. Overlays need to be composited **on top** of `[vfinal]` using ffmpeg's `overlay` filter.

**Strategy**: After producing `[vfinal]` from the concat, chain overlay filters sequentially. Each overlay becomes:

```
[input_idx:v] scale=W:H, format=rgba, colorchannelmixer=aa=OPACITY [ovl_i_scaled];
[prev_video][ovl_i_scaled] overlay=x=X:y=Y:enable='between(t,START,END)' [ovl_i_out]
```

Implementation steps in `build_ffmpeg_command`:

a. **Collect overlay clips** alongside video/audio clips (add `overlay_clips` list filtered from `all_clips`).

b. **Register overlay assets as inputs** using the existing `get_input_idx` mechanism. Image assets already get `-loop 1` prepended.

c. **After building `[vfinal]`**, iterate through overlay clips sorted by `at` time:
   - For each overlay, create a scale filter for the overlay image/video to the specified `width`x`height`.
   - If the overlay source is a video (not an image), apply `trim` for the `from`/`to` range.
   - If `opacity < 1.0`, add `format=rgba,colorchannelmixer=aa={opacity}`.
   - Apply `overlay=x={x}:y={y}:enable='between(t,{at},{at+duration})'` on top of the current video label.
   - Chain the output as the new "current" video label.

d. **The final label after all overlays** replaces `vfinal` in the `-map` output.

e. For the `enable` expression: `at` is the timeline position, and `at + clip_timeline_duration(clip)` is the end. The `between(t,...)` function in ffmpeg operates on the output timeline PTS which aligns with the concat output.

**Important edge case**: The `enable` parameter on the overlay filter is critical -- it means the overlay input is only composited during its time range. Without it, the overlay would appear for the entire video. Using `enable` avoids needing to restructure the concat pipeline.

### 3. Viewer: Timeline Data Parsing (`timeline-data.ts`)

a. **Extend `RawClip`** to include overlay fields:
   ```
   track: 'video' | 'audio' | 'overlay'
   x?: number
   y?: number
   width?: number
   height?: number
   opacity?: number
   ```

b. **Extend `ClipMeta`** with the same overlay fields.

c. **Add a third row** in `buildFromRaw`: `{ id: 'row-overlay', actions: overlayActions }`.

d. **Update `toYaml`** to serialize overlay clips back, including the `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `opacity` fields. Add `'row-overlay': 'overlay'` to `trackOrder`.

e. **Update `ROW_LABELS`** in `App.tsx` to include `'row-overlay': 'Overlay'`.

### 4. Viewer: LivePreview Overlay Rendering

The preview currently draws video frames to a canvas. Overlays need to be drawn **on top** after the video frame.

a. **Preload overlay image assets**: In the existing `useEffect` that creates `<video>` and `<audio>` elements, also create `<img>` elements for overlay image assets and store them in a new ref (`overlayImages`). For video overlays, reuse the video element pool.

b. **New `drawOverlays(time)` function**: After `drawVideoFrame` (or `drawTranscript`) completes:
   - Find all overlay clips active at the current time (`clips.filter(c => c.track === 'overlay' && time >= c.start && time < c.end)`).
   - For each, compute the canvas-space position by mapping from output resolution (1280x720) to actual canvas display size. The canvas is 1280x720 logical pixels but is CSS-scaled with letterboxing. Since the canvas logical size matches output resolution, the overlay `x`/`y`/`width`/`height` map directly to `ctx.drawImage(img, x, y, width, height)`.
   - Apply opacity via `ctx.globalAlpha = overlay.opacity` before drawing, then restore.
   - Draw overlays in clip order (later clips on top).

c. **Integrate into render loop**: Modify `syncVideo` to call `drawOverlays(time)` after drawing the video frame. Also call it after `drawTranscript` (overlays should appear even during gaps).

### 5. Viewer: Interactive Overlay Editing on Canvas

This is the most complex UI addition. The goal is drag-to-move and resize handles on the preview canvas.

a. **New component `OverlayEditor`**: A transparent div layered on top of the canvas (via absolute positioning in the `.live-preview` container). This avoids interfering with canvas drawing.

b. **Selection state**: Track which overlay clip is selected (click to select). Show a selection border with 8 resize handles (corners + edges).

c. **Coordinate mapping**: The canvas CSS size differs from its logical size (1280x720). Compute the scale factor and offset from the canvas element's `getBoundingClientRect()` vs its logical dimensions. All mouse events need to be transformed from screen space to output-resolution space.

d. **Drag behavior**:
   - `onMouseDown` on an overlay: start drag, record offset from overlay origin.
   - `onMouseMove`: update the overlay's `x`/`y` in meta, call `applyTimelineEdit` to propagate changes.
   - `onMouseUp`: finalize position.

e. **Resize behavior**:
   - `onMouseDown` on a resize handle: track which handle and the initial dimensions.
   - `onMouseMove`: compute new `width`/`height` (and possibly `x`/`y` for top/left handles). Optionally hold Shift for aspect-ratio lock.
   - `onMouseUp`: finalize.

f. **Integration with App.tsx**: 
   - Pass overlay clips, meta, and `applyTimelineEdit` callback to the `OverlayEditor`.
   - The `OverlayEditor` only shows overlays active at `currentTime`.
   - When an overlay is dragged/resized, it calls `applyTimelineEdit` with updated meta containing the new `x`/`y`/`width`/`height`.

g. **Visual indicators**: Draw semi-transparent overlay boundaries even when not selected, with a brighter border on hover. Selected overlay gets resize handles.

### 6. Changes to `view.py` (Text View Tool)

Update `compute_timeline_positions` and `render_view` to handle `track: overlay` clips. Display them as a separate section in the text output showing asset, position, size, and time range.

### 7. Implementation Sequence

1. **`timeline-data.ts`** -- Add overlay types and parsing (row, meta fields, serialization). Low risk, foundational.
2. **`timeline.yaml`** -- Add a sample overlay clip for testing.
3. **`App.tsx`** -- Add the overlay row label and pass overlay data through. Minor changes.
4. **`LivePreview.tsx`** -- Add overlay image preloading and `drawOverlays()` into the render loop. Medium complexity.
5. **`render.py`** -- Add overlay filter chain after `[vfinal]`. Medium complexity, testable with `--dry-run`.
6. **New `OverlayEditor.tsx`** -- Interactive drag/resize component. Highest complexity, can be done last since the feature works without interactive editing (you can set x/y/width/height in YAML manually).
7. **`App.css`** -- Styles for overlay selection, handles, and the overlay row.
8. **`view.py`** -- Minor update to display overlay clips in text view.

### 8. Potential Challenges

- **FFmpeg `enable` timing**: The `between(t,...)` expression operates on the output stream's PTS. After concat, PTS should be continuous from 0, but this needs verification. If not, `setpts=PTS-STARTPTS` on the concat output may be needed.
- **Multiple overlays at same time**: FFmpeg overlay filters must be chained sequentially (each takes the output of the previous). Order matters for z-stacking.
- **Canvas coordinate mapping for interactive editing**: The CSS-scaled canvas means mouse coordinates need careful transformation. The canvas is 1280x720 logical but may display at any CSS size with letterboxing.
- **Video overlays (not just images)**: If an overlay asset is a video, the preview needs to seek and play it similarly to the main video track. This adds significant complexity. Recommend starting with image-only overlays and adding video overlay support as a follow-up.
- **Performance**: Drawing multiple overlay images per frame in the RAF loop should be fine for a few overlays. The `drawImage` call on pre-loaded `<img>` elements is fast.

---

- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/announcement-video/tools/render.py` - FFmpeg rendering: add overlay filter chain after [vfinal] concat using overlay=x:y:enable=between(t,start,end)
