{
  "file_path": "/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/announcement-video/scripts/make_venn_animated_alpha.py",
  "content": "from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont, ImageChops\nimport subprocess, os, math\n\nW, H = 1920, 1080\nFPS = 30\nOUT_DIR = \"/tmp/venn_frames_alpha\"\nos.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)\n\nSCRIPT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))\nINPUT_DIR = os.path.join(SCRIPT_DIR, \"..\", \"inputs\")\n\n# Circle params\nr = 280\ncx1 = W // 2 - 160\ncx2 = W // 2 + 160\ncy = H // 2 - 30\n\n# Colors (all RGBA for transparent compositing)\nleft_fill = (60, 130, 200, 80)\nright_fill = (200, 80, 60, 80)\nleft_outline = (80, 160, 240, 255)\nright_outline = (240, 100, 80, 255)\nlabel_color_l = (180, 210, 255, 255)\nlabel_color_r = (255, 180, 170, 255)\narrow_color = (220, 200, 100, 255)\nflash_color = (255, 240, 140, 120)\n\n# Font\ntry:\n    font_big = ImageFont.truetype(\"/System/Library/Fonts/Helvetica.ttc\", 38)\n    font_med = ImageFont.truetype(\"/System/Library/Fonts/Helvetica.ttc\", 30)\n    font_label = ImageFont.truetype(\"/System/Library/Fonts/Helvetica.ttc\", 28)\nexcept Exception:\n    font_big = ImageFont.load_default()\n    font_med = font_big\n    font_label = font_big\n\n\ndef ease_out(t):\n    return 1 - (1 - t) ** 3\n\n\ndef alpha_scale(color, frac):\n    \"\"\"Scale the alpha channel of an RGBA color.\"\"\"\n    return (color[0], color[1], color[2], int(color[3] * frac))\n\n\ndef draw_circle_left(draw, alpha=1.0):\n    fill = alpha_scale(left_fill, alpha)\n    outline = alpha_scale(left_outline, alpha)\n    draw.ellipse([cx1 - r, cy - r, cx1 + r, cy + r], fill=fill, outline=outline, width=3)\n    tc = alpha_scale(label_color_l, alpha)\n    t1, t2 = \"Creative\", \"Control\"\n    bb1 = draw.textbbox((0, 0), t1, font=font_big)\n    bb2 = draw.textbbox((0, 0), t2, font=font_med)\n    lx = cx1 - 70\n    draw.text((lx - (bb1[2] - bb1[0]) // 2, cy - 30), t1, fill=tc, font=font_big)\n    draw.text((lx - (bb2[2] - bb2[0]) // 2, cy + 15), t2, fill=tc, font=font_med)\n\n\ndef draw_circle_right(draw, alpha=1.0):\n    fill = alpha_scale(right_fill, alpha)\n    outline = alpha_scale(right_outline, alpha)\n    draw.ellipse([cx2 - r, cy - r, cx2 + r, cy + r], fill=fill, outline=outline, width=3)\n    tc = alpha_scale(label_color_r, alpha)\n    t1, t2 = \"Model\", \"Creativity\"\n    bb1 = draw.textbbox((0, 0), t1, font=font_big)\n    bb2 = draw.textbbox((0, 0), t2, font=font_med)\n    rx = cx2 + 70\n    draw.text((rx - (bb1[2] - bb1[0]) // 2, cy - 30), t1, fill=tc, font=font_big)\n    draw.text((rx - (bb2[2] - bb2[0]) // 2, cy + 15), t2, fill=tc, font=font_med)\n\n\ndef draw_label(draw, alpha=1.0):\n    tc = alpha_scale(arrow_color, alpha)\n    text = \"Using Anchor Images\"\n    bb = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font_label)\n    tw = bb[2] - bb[0]\n    draw.text((W // 2 - tw // 2, cy + r + 95), text, fill=tc, font=font_label)\n\n\ndef draw_arrow(draw, progress=1.0, alpha=1.0):\n    tc = alpha_scale(arrow_color, alpha)\n    overlap_x = W // 2\n    start_y = cy + r + 80\n    end_y = cy\n    current_end_y = int(start_y + (end_y - start_y) * progress)\n    draw.line([(overlap_x, start_y), (overlap_x, current_end_y)], fill=tc, width=3)\n    hs = 12\n    draw.polygon([\n        (overlap_x, current_end_y),\n        (overlap_x - hs, current_end_y + int(hs * 1.5)),\n        (overlap_x + hs, current_end_y + int(hs * 1.5)),\n    ], fill=tc)\n\n\ndef draw_intersection_flash(alpha=1.0):\n    m1 = Image.new(\"L\", (W, H), 0)\n    ImageDraw.Draw(m1).ellipse([cx1 - r, cy - r, cx1 + r, cy + r], fill=255)\n    m2 = Image.new(\"L\", (W, H), 0)\n    ImageDraw.Draw(m2).ellipse([cx2 - r, cy - r, cx2 + r, cy + r], fill=255)\n    intersection = ImageChops.multiply(m1, m2)\n    intersection = intersection.point(lambda p: int(p * alpha))\n    flash = Image.new(\"RGBA\", (W, H), (0, 0, 0, 0))\n    flash_solid = Image.new(\"RGBA\", (W, H), flash_color)\n    flash.paste(flash_solid, mask=intersection)\n    return flash\n\n\n# Timeline (seconds):\n# 0.0-0.3: empty\n# 0.3-0.7: left circle appears\n# 0.7-1.2: hold\n# 1.2-1.6: right circle appears\n# 1.6-2.1: hold\n# 2.1-2.5: label text appears\n# 2.5-3.2: arrow grows upward\n# 3.2-3.8: intersection flashes\n# 3.8-5.0: hold final\n\ntotal_frames = FPS * 5\n\nfor f in range(total_frames):\n    t = f / FPS\n\n    # Transparent background\n    img = Image.new(\"RGBA\", (W, H), (0, 0, 0, 0))\n    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img, \"RGBA\")\n\n    left_a = 0 if t < 0.3 else (ease_out((t - 0.3) / 0.4) if t < 0.7 else 1.0)\n    right_a = 0 if t < 1.2 else (ease_out((t - 1.2) / 0.4) if t < 1.6 else 1.0)\n    label_a = 0 if t < 2.1 else (ease_out((t - 2.1) / 0.4) if t < 2.5 else 1.0)\n    arrow_prog = 0 if t < 2.5 else (ease_out((t - 2.5) / 0.7) if t < 3.2 else 1.0)\n\n    if t < 3.2:\n        flash_a = 0\n    elif t < 3.5:\n        flash_a = ease_out((t - 3.2) / 0.3)\n    elif t < 3.8:\n        flash_a = max(1.0 - (t - 3.5) / 0.3, 0.3)\n    else:\n        flash_a = 0.3\n\n    if left_a > 0:\n        draw_circle_left(draw, left_a)\n    if right_a > 0:\n        draw_circle_right(draw, right_a)\n    if label_a > 0:\n        draw_label(draw, label_a)\n    if arrow_prog > 0:\n        draw_arrow(draw, arrow_prog, label_a)\n    if flash_a > 0:\n        flash_layer = draw_intersection_flash(flash_a)\n        img = Image.alpha_composite(img, flash_layer)\n\n    img.save(os.path.join(OUT_DIR, f\"frame_{f:04d}.png\"))\n\nprint(f\"Generated {total_frames} frames in {OUT_DIR}\")\n\n# Encode to WebM VP9 with alpha\noutput = os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, \"venn_diagram_video.webm\")\ncmd = [\n    \"ffmpeg\", \"-y\",\n    \"-framerate\", str(FPS),\n    \"-i\", os.path.join(OUT_DIR, \"frame_%04d.png\"),\n    \"-c:v\", \"libvpx-vp9\",\n    \"-pix_fmt\", \"yuva420p\",\n    \"-b:v\", \"2M\",\n    \"-auto-alt-ref\", \"0\",\n    output,\n]\nprint(f\"Encoding → {output}\")\nsubprocess.run(cmd, check=True)\nprint(\"Done!\")\n"
}

1. Make gap fills transparent (`color=c=black@0.0` with `format=rgba`)
2. Add `format=rgba` to video processing so alpha is preserved through concat
3. The pad color needs to be transparent too

> AGENT

The pipeline looks correct:
- All video segments use `format=rgba` and `pad` with `color=black@0.0` (transparent)
- Gaps use `color=c=black@0.0` (transparent) 
- The webm inputs with alpha are read by ffmpeg
- Everything gets concatenated with alpha preserved, then `[vfinal]` is scaled down and overlaid on `[bg]`
- Final output is still `yuv420p` H.264 (no alpha needed in the final render since the background fills it)

  "new_string": "  const clearBuffer = useCallback(() => {\n    const { buf, ctx } = getBuffer()\n    if (backgroundScale < 1) {\n      // Transparent so background shows through\n      ctx.clearRect(0, 0, buf.width, buf.height)\n    } else {\n      ctx.fillStyle = '#000'\n      ctx.fillRect(0, 0, buf.width, buf.height)\n    }\n  }, [getBuffer, backgroundScale])\n\n  const drawBlack = useCallback(() => {\n    clearBuffer()\n  }, [clearBuffer])"
}

> AGENT

Fixed. The problem was that all draw functions filled the buffer with opaque black before drawing the video frame, which destroyed the alpha channel. Now:

- `clearBuffer()` uses `clearRect` (transparent) when there's a background, or `fillRect` with black when there isn't
- `drawVideoFrame`, `drawTranscript`, and `drawBlack` all go through `clearBuffer()`
- Transparent pixels from the WebM videos are preserved in the buffer, so when `compositeToCanvas()` draws the buffer onto the background, those areas show through

Refresh the viewer and it should match what the render output looks like.

> DEVELOPER

And see the background image thing and the position of the videos on top of it, is that done in a flexible way that I can vary it by asset, you know so I can zoom in one and zoom out another? This is a well engineered

> AGENT

No, it's not flexible right now. There's a single `background_scale: 0.95` that applies uniformly to all content. You can't have the composition at 90% and the venn diagram at 100% — everything gets the same scale.

To do it per-clip, the scale would need to be a property on each clip in the timeline, not a global output setting. And the pipeline would need to change — instead of scaling `[vfinal]` as a whole at the end, each clip segment would need its own scale applied before concat, with the background composited per-segment.

Want me to add per-clip `scale` support?

Now I have a clear picture. Currently:

1. **Single audio element** — `audioElement` is a single ref, only the first audio asset gets created
2. **No volume support** — `ClipMeta` has no `volume` field
3. **Single audio row** — only one `row-audio` track
4. **`findClipAt` returns only one clip** — can't handle multiple simultaneous audio clips
5. **render.py** already supports `volume` per clip

I need to:
1. Add `volume` to `ClipMeta` and `RawClip`
2. Support multiple audio rows (e.g. `row-audio-1`, `row-audio-2`)
3. Change `audioElement` to a map like `videoElements`
4. Rewrite `syncAudio` to handle multiple simultaneous audio clips
5. Parse/serialize volume in timeline-data.ts
6. Update render.py audio handling if needed

> AGENT

Good. Now to use it, you add audio clips to `timeline.yaml` with `volume`:

```yaml
clips:
  # Main voiceover
  - at: 4.63
    track: audio
    asset: input
    from: 0
    to: 113.77
    volume: 0.8
  # Background music
  - at: 0
    track: audio
    asset: music
    from: 0
    to: 120
    volume: 0.3
```

Here's what changed:

- **Multiple audio layers**: Each unique audio asset gets its own timeline row, so you can have voiceover and music playing simultaneously
- **Per-clip volume**: Add `volume: 0.3` (0-1) to any audio clip in the YAML. Defaults to 1.0
- **Preview**: Each audio asset gets its own `<audio>` element with `volume` set, all synced independently
- **Render**: Audio layers are built separately (concat within each layer), then mixed together with `amix` using `normalize=0` so your volume values are respected exactly
- **Track labels**: Audio rows show the asset name instead of generic "Audio"

# Claude Code for Video Creation with Prompting

## Overview
This guide demonstrates how to create videos through prompting using Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI tool. The approach leverages AI to streamline video production for beginners.

## Essential Requirements
Two installations are necessary: Claude Code (requires paid subscription) and Node.js runtime environment.

## Project Setup Process

**Initialize a new project:**
```bash
npx create-video@latest
```

The recommended configuration includes selecting the Blank template, enabling TailwindCSS support, and installing the Skills feature.

## Running Your Project

**Navigate to your project folder and prepare it:**
```bash
cd my-video
npm install
npm run dev
```

This launches the development preview.

**Activate Claude in a separate terminal:**
```bash
cd my-video
claude
```

Once running, you can begin prompting to generate video content. The accompanying tutorial video (5 minutes) provides practical examples for motion graphics creation suitable for newcomers to video development.

This approach simplifies the video creation workflow by allowing natural language prompts to generate motion graphics, making Remotion accessible to users without extensive technical experience.

1→#!/bin/bash
     2→# Creates the composition video with transparent background:
     3→# image1 (top-left) + image2 (bottom-left) + video (right)
     4→# Images fade in sequentially, then the video fades in and plays
     5→# Output: WebM VP9 with alpha channel
     6→
     7→SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
     8→INPUT_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/../inputs"
     9→
    10→ffmpeg -y \
    11→  -f lavfi -i "color=c=black@0.0:s=1920x1080:d=7,format=rgba" \
    12→  -loop 1 -t 7 -i "$INPUT_DIR/example-image1.jpg" \
    13→  -loop 1 -t 7 -i "$INPUT_DIR/example-image2.jpg" \
    14→  -i "$INPUT_DIR/example-video.mp4" \
    15→  -filter_complex "\
    16→    [1:v]scale=640:476,format=rgba,fade=t=in:st=0:d=0.4:alpha=1[img1];\
    17→    [2:v]scale=640:476,format=rgba,fade=t=in:st=0.5:d=0.4:alpha=1[img2];\
    18→    [3:v]scale=1160:876,format=rgba,setpts=PTS+1.0/TB,fade=t=in:st=1.0:d=0.4:alpha=1[vid];\
    19→    [0:v][img1]overlay=40:54[t1];\
    20→    [t1][img2]overlay=40:550[t2];\
    21→    [t2][vid]overlay=720:102:eof_action=pass[out]\
    22→  " \
    23→  -map "[out]" \
    24→  -t 6.37 \
    25→  -c:v libvpx-vp9 -pix_fmt yuva420p -b:v 4M -auto-alt-ref 0 \
    26→  "$INPUT_DIR/output_composition.webm"
    27→
```

> AGENT

So the composition is:
- 1920x1080, ~6.37 seconds, transparent background
- **image1** (640x476) at position (40, 54), fades in over 0.4s starting at t=0
- **image2** (640x476) at position (40, 550), fades in over 0.4s starting at t=0.5
- **video** (1160x876) at position (720, 102), fades in over 0.4s starting at t=1.0, plays from 0

  "content": "import {\n  AbsoluteFill,\n  Img,\n  OffthreadVideo,\n  interpolate,\n  useCurrentFrame,\n  staticFile,\n} from \"remotion\";\n\nconst FPS = 30;\n\n// Fade in helper: returns opacity 0→1 over `duration` seconds starting at `startSec`\nfunction fadeIn(frame: number, startSec: number, durationSec: number): number {\n  const startFrame = Math.round(startSec * FPS);\n  const durationFrames = Math.round(durationSec * FPS);\n  return interpolate(frame, [startFrame, startFrame + durationFrames], [0, 1], {\n    extrapolateLeft: \"clamp\",\n    extrapolateRight: \"clamp\",\n  });\n}\n\nexport const CompositionVideo: React.FC = () => {\n  const frame = useCurrentFrame();\n\n  // Image 1: top-left, fades in at t=0 over 0.4s\n  const img1Opacity = fadeIn(frame, 0, 0.4);\n\n  // Image 2: bottom-left, fades in at t=0.5 over 0.4s\n  const img2Opacity = fadeIn(frame, 0.5, 0.4);\n\n  // Video: right side, fades in at t=1.0 over 0.4s\n  const vidOpacity = fadeIn(frame, 1.0, 0.4);\n\n  return (\n    <AbsoluteFill style={{ backgroundColor: \"transparent\" }}>\n      {/* Image 1: top-left */}\n      <Img\n        src={staticFile(\"example-image1.jpg\")}\n        style={{\n          position: \"absolute\",\n          left: 40,\n          top: 54,\n          width: 640,\n          height: 476,\n          opacity: img1Opacity,\n        }}\n      />\n\n      {/* Image 2: bottom-left */}\n      <Img\n        src={staticFile(\"example-image2.jpg\")}\n        style={{\n          position: \"absolute\",\n          left: 40,\n          top: 550,\n          width: 640,\n          height: 476,\n          opacity: img2Opacity,\n        }}\n      />\n\n      {/* Video: right side */}\n      <div\n        style={{\n          position: \"absolute\",\n          left: 720,\n          top: 102,\n          width: 1160,\n          height: 876,\n          opacity: vidOpacity,\n          overflow: \"hidden\",\n        }}\n      >\n        <OffthreadVideo\n          src={staticFile(\"example-video.mp4\")}\n          style={{\n            width: \"100%\",\n            height: \"100%\",\n            objectFit: \"cover\",\n          }}\n          muted\n        />\n      </div>\n    </AbsoluteFill>\n  );\n};\n"
}

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Offscreen buffer canvas pattern**: All draw functions target a hidden canvas at full 1280x720, then `compositeToCanvas()` handles background + scale compositing onto the visible canvas. Mirrors render.py's pipeline exactly.
   - **Alpha transparency pipeline**: WebM VP9 with yuva420p for video assets with transparent backgrounds. ffmpeg uses `format=rgba`, `color=black@0.0` for transparent gaps, `pad` with transparent color.
   - **Multi-layer audio**: Each unique audio asset gets its own timeline row. In render.py, layers are concatenated separately then mixed with `amix`. In the preview, each asset gets its own `<audio>` element with independent volume.
   - **Background compositing**: Configurable via `background_scale` in timeline.yaml output config. Single source of truth read by both render.py and the viewer.
   - **Remotion**: React-based video framework. Used to recreate the composition video with `AbsoluteFill`, `Img`, `OffthreadVideo`, and `interpolate` for fade animations. Renders to WebM VP8 with alpha.

     - Core preview component. Major rewrite to use offscreen buffer pattern, transparent clearing, and multi-audio support.
     - Key changes: `bufferCanvas` ref for offscreen drawing, `clearBuffer()` for transparent/black clearing based on `backgroundScale`, `audioElements` map (replacing single `audioElement`), `activeAudioClips` Set, `findAudioClipsAt()` for multi-clip support, `syncAudio` handles simultaneous clips with volume.

     ```typescript
     interface Props {
       rows: TimelineRow[]
       meta: Record<string, ClipMeta>
       assetPaths: Record<string, string>
       transcript: TranscriptSegment[]
       background?: string
       backgroundScale?: number
       onTimeUpdate: (time: number) => void
     }

     - Buffer pattern:
     ```typescript
     const bufferCanvas = useRef<HTMLCanvasElement>(document.createElement('canvas'))
     // All draw functions use getBuffer() to target the offscreen canvas
     const getBuffer = useCallback(() => {
       const buf = bufferCanvas.current
       return { buf, ctx: buf.getContext('2d')! }
     }, [])
     ```
     - clearBuffer for transparency:
     ```typescript
     const clearBuffer = useCallback(() => {
       const { buf, ctx } = getBuffer()
       if (backgroundScale < 1) {
         ctx.clearRect(0, 0, buf.width, buf.height)
       } else {
         ctx.fillStyle = '#000'
         ctx.fillRect(0, 0, buf.width, buf.height)
       }
     }, [getBuffer, backgroundScale])
     ```
     - compositeToCanvas:
     ```typescript
     const compositeToCanvas = useCallback(() => {
       const canvas = canvasRef.current
       if (!canvas) return
       const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d')
       if (!ctx) return
       const W = canvas.width
       const H = canvas.height
       const buf = bufferCanvas.current
       const bg = bgImage.current
       if (bg && bg.complete && bg.naturalWidth > 0 && backgroundScale < 1) {
         ctx.drawImage(bg, 0, 0, W, H)
         const cw = Math.round(W * backgroundScale)
         const ch = Math.round(H * backgroundScale)
         const cx = Math.round((W - cw) / 2)
         const cy = Math.round((H - ch) / 2)
         ctx.drawImage(buf, cx, cy, cw, ch)
       } else {
         ctx.drawImage(buf, 0, 0)
       }
     }, [backgroundScale])
     ```
     - Multi-audio syncAudio:
     ```typescript
     const syncAudio = useCallback(
       (time: number, shouldPlay: boolean) => {
         const activeClips = findAudioClipsAt(time)
         const activeIds = new Set(activeClips.map(c => c.actionId))
         for (const prevId of activeAudioClips.current) {
           if (!activeIds.has(prevId)) {
             const prevClip = clips.find(c => c.actionId === prevId)
             if (prevClip) audioElements.current[prevClip.asset]?.pause()
           }
         }
         for (const clip of activeClips) {
           const aud = audioElements.current[clip.asset]
           if (!aud) continue
           const sourceTime = getSourceTime(clip, time)
           aud.volume = clip.volume
           if (shouldPlay) {
             if (!activeAudioClips.current.has(clip.actionId) || Math.abs(aud.currentTime - sourceTime) > 0.3) {
               aud.currentTime = sourceTime
             }
             if (aud.paused) aud.play()
           } else {
             aud.currentTime = sourceTime
             aud.pause()
           }
         }
         activeAudioClips.current = activeIds
       },
       [findAudioClipsAt, clips],
     )
     ```

   - **OverlayEditor canvasRef inline object**: Passed `{ current: previewRef.current?.canvasElement ?? null }` which creates new object every render. Fixed by creating a proper `canvasRef = useRef<HTMLCanvasElement | null>(null)` in App.tsx and syncing via useEffect.
   - **Overlay positioning broken (user feedback: "is this well-engineered?")**: Overlays drew at full-canvas coords but video was in scaled area. Fixed by adopting offscreen buffer pattern where everything draws at full 1280x720, then compositeToCanvas handles the background+scale.
   - **Magic number 0.95 duplicated**: Was hardcoded in both LivePreview (`CONTENT_SCALE`) and render.py. Fixed by making it configurable as `background_scale` in timeline.yaml, read by both.
   - **Transparent backgrounds not showing in preview (user: "not showing transparent in the video")**: `drawVideoFrame`/`drawTranscript` filled buffer with opaque black (`ctx.fillRect` with '#000') before drawing video, destroying alpha channel. Fixed with `clearBuffer()` that uses `ctx.clearRect` (transparent) when `backgroundScale < 1`.
   - **Remotion "does not contain registerRoot"**: Entry point `src/index.ts` only exported RemotionRoot. Fixed by adding `import { registerRoot } from "remotion"; registerRoot(RemotionRoot);`

5. Problem Solving:
   - Architecture quality review led to offscreen buffer pattern that mirrors render.py pipeline exactly (draw all content → scale → composite on background)
   - Alpha transparency required coordinated changes across: video asset generation (WebM VP9), render.py (format=rgba, transparent gaps/padding), and LivePreview (clearRect instead of fillRect)
   - Multi-audio support required changing from single element to map of elements, single active clip tracking to Set-based tracking, and render.py from sequential concat to per-layer concat + amix

    76→export async function loadTranscript(assetKey: string, assetPath: string): Promise<TranscriptSegment[]> {
    77→  const filename = assetPath.split('/').pop() ?? ''
    78→  const ext = filename.includes('.') ? filename.slice(filename.lastIndexOf('.')) : ''
    79→
    80→  // Try filename first, then asset key + extension
    81→  for (const name of [filename, `${assetKey}${ext}`]) {
    82→    const res = await fetch(`/media/asset_profiles/${name}.yaml`)
    83→    if (!res.ok) continue
    84→    const text = await res.text()
    85→    const profile = yaml.load(text) as { transcript?: { segments?: TranscriptSegment[] } }
    86→    const segments = profile?.transcript?.segments
    87→    if (segments?.length) return segments
    88→  }
    89→  return []
    90→}

    92→function buildFromRaw(timeline: RawTimeline): TimelineData {

    96→    if (!effects[effectId]) {
    97→      effects[effectId] = { id: effectId }
    98→    }
    99→  }

   105→
   106→  // Track audio row assignment: each unique asset gets its own row
   107→  let audioRowCounter = 0
   108→  const assetToAudioRow: Record<string, string> = {}
   109→
   110→  for (const [i, clip] of timeline.clips.entries()) {
   111→    const speed = clip.speed ?? 1
   112→    let duration: number
   113→    if (clip.track === 'overlay' && clip.hold != null) {
   114→      duration = clip.hold
   115→    } else {
   116→      duration = (clip.to - clip.from) / speed
   117→    }
   118→    const action: TimelineAction = {
   119→      id: `clip-${i}`,
   120→      start: clip.at,
   121→      end: clip.at + duration,
   122→      effectId: `effect-${clip.asset}`,
   123→    }
   124→    meta[action.id] = {
   125→      asset: clip.asset,
   126→      track: clip.track,
   127→      from: clip.from ?? 0,
   128→      to: clip.to ?? (clip.hold ?? 0),
   129→      speed,
   130→      volume: clip.volume ?? 1.0,
   131→      x: clip.x ?? 0,

   133→      width: clip.width ?? 320,
   134→      height: clip.height ?? 240,
   135→      opacity: clip.opacity ?? 1.0,
   136→    }
   137→    if (clip.track === 'video') {
   138→      videoActions.push(action)
   139→    } else if (clip.track === 'overlay') {
   140→      overlayActions.push(action)
   141→    } else {
   142→      // Assign each audio asset to its own row for multi-track support
   143→      if (!assetToAudioRow[clip.asset]) {
   144→        assetToAudioRow[clip.asset] = `row-audio-${audioRowCounter++}`
   145→      }
   146→      const rowId = assetToAudioRow[clip.asset]
   147→      if (!audioRowMap[rowId]) audioRowMap[rowId] = []
   148→      audioRowMap[rowId].push(action)
   149→    }
   150→  }
   151→
   152→  const audioRows: TimelineRow[] = Object.entries(audioRowMap).map(
   153→    ([id, actions]) => ({ id, actions })
   154→  )
   155→
   156→  return {
   157→    rows: [
   158→      { id: 'row-video', actions: videoActions },
   159→      ...audioRows,
   160→      { id: 'row-overlay', actions: overlayActions },
   161→    ],
   162→    meta,

   169→// Parse yaml text into timeline data
   170→export function parseTimeline(text: string): TimelineData {
   171→  const timeline = yaml.load(text) as RawTimeline
   172→  return buildFromRaw(timeline)
   173→}
   174→
   175→// Convert editor state back to YAML string
   176→export function toYaml(
   177→  rows: TimelineRow[],
   178→  meta: Record<string, ClipMeta>,
   179→  header: TimelineData['header'],
   180→): string {
   181→  const clips: RawClip[] = []
   182→
   183→  function rowTrack(rowId: string): 'video' | 'audio' | 'overlay' | null {
   184→    if (rowId === 'row-video') return 'video'
   185→    if (rowId.startsWith('row-audio')) return 'audio'
   186→    if (rowId === 'row-overlay') return 'overlay'
   187→    return null
   188→  }
   189→
   190→  for (const row of rows) {
   191→    const track = rowTrack(row.id)
   192→    if (!track) continue
   193→    const sorted = [...row.actions].sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start)
   194→    for (const action of sorted) {
   195→      const m = meta[action.id]
   196→      if (!m) continue
   197→
   198→      if (track === 'overlay') {
   199→        const clip: RawClip = {
   200→          at: round(action.start),
   201→          track,
   202→          asset: m.asset,
   203→          from: 0,
   204→          to: 0,
   205→          hold: round(action.end - action.start),
   206→          x: round(m.x),
   207→          y: round(m.y),
   208→          width: round(m.width),
   209→          height: round(m.height),
   210→          opacity: round(m.opacity),
   211→        }
   212→        clips.push(clip)
   213→      } else {
   214→        const clip: RawClip = {
   215→          at: round(action.start),
   216→          track,
   217→          asset: m.asset,
   218→          from: round(m.from),
   219→          to: round(getSourceTime({ from: m.from, start: action.start, speed: m.speed }, action.end)),
   220→        }
   221→        if (m.speed !== 1) {
   222→          clip.speed = round(m.speed)
   223→        }
   224→        if (track === 'audio' && m.volume !== 1) {
   225→          clip.volume = round(m.volume)
   226→        }
   227→        clips.push(clip)
   228→      }
   229→    }
   230→  }
   231→
   232→  const doc = {
   233→    output: header.output,
   234→    asset_map: header.asset_map,
   235→    clips,
   236→  }
   237→
   238→  return yaml.dump(doc, {
   239→    lineWidth: -1,
   240→    noRefs: true,
   241→    quotingType: '"',
   242→    forceQuotes: false,
   243→  })
   244→}
   245→
   246→function round(n: number): number {
   247→  return Math.round(n * 100) / 100

    51→  const [renderDirty, setRenderDirty] = useState(false)
    52→  const saveTimer = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>(null)
    53→  const headerRef = useRef<TimelineData['header'] | null>(null)
    54→
    55→  // Ref always holds the latest meta, so save callbacks don't need it as a dep
    56→  const metaRef = useRef(meta)
    57→  metaRef.current = meta
    58→
    59→  // Suppress onChange saves during poll-triggered state updates.

    61→  useEffect(() => {
    62→    ignoreNextOnChange.current = false
    63→  })
    64→
    65→  // ── Single update path for all timeline edits ─────────────────────────────
    66→  // Every edit (drag, resize, poll) flows through here.
    67→
    68→  const saveToYaml = useCallback(async (currentRows: TimelineRow[]) => {
    69→    if (!headerRef.current) return
    70→    setSaveStatus('saving')
    71→    try {
    72→      const yamlStr = toYaml(currentRows, metaRef.current, headerRef.current)
    73→      lastYaml.current = yamlStr

    76→        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/yaml' },

    87→    }

    95→
    96→  /**
    97→   * Central update function. All edits to rows/meta go through here.
    98→   * Ensures state is set, save is scheduled, and preview is refreshed.
    99→   */
   100→  const applyTimelineEdit = useCallback((
   101→    newRows: TimelineRow[],
   102→    metaUpdates?: Record<string, Partial<ClipMeta>>,
   103→  ) => {
   104→    setRows(newRows)
   105→
   106→    if (metaUpdates && Object.keys(metaUpdates).length > 0) {
   107→      setMeta(prev => {
   108→        const next = { ...prev }
   109→        for (const [id, patch] of Object.entries(metaUpdates)) {
   110→          if (next[id]) {
   111→            next[id] = { ...next[id], ...patch }
   112→          }
   113→        }
   114→        return next
   115→      })
   116→    }
   117→
   118→    scheduleSave(newRows)

   120→    queueMicrotask(() => previewRef.current?.refresh())
   121→  }, [scheduleSave])
   122→
   123→  // Keep canvasRef in sync with the preview's canvas element
   124→  useEffect(() => {
   125→    canvasRef.current = previewRef.current?.canvasElement ?? null
   126→  })
   127→
   128→  // ── Poll for external yaml changes ────────────────────────────────────────
   129→
   130→  const lastYaml = useRef('')
   131→  useEffect(() => {
   132→    const poll = async () => {
   133→      try {
   134→        const res = await fetch('/api/timeline')
   135→        const text = await res.text()
   136→        if (text !== lastYaml.current) {
   137→          lastYaml.current = text
   138→          const d = parseTimeline(text)
   139→          ignoreNextOnChange.current = true
   140→          setData(d)
   141→          setRows(d.rows)
   142→          setMeta({ ...d.meta })
   143→          headerRef.current = d.header
   144→          setRenderDirty(true)
   145→        }
   146→      } catch {}
   147→    }
   148→    poll()
   149→    const id = setInterval(poll, 1000)
   150→    return () => clearInterval(id)
   151→  }, [])
   152→
   153→  // Load transcript once when data first available
   154→  const transcriptLoaded = useRef(false)
   155→  useEffect(() => {
   156→    if (!data || transcriptLoaded.current) return
   157→    const audioMeta = Object.values(data.meta).find(m => m.track === 'audio')
   158→    if (!audioMeta) return
   159→    const assetPath = data.assetMap[audioMeta.asset]
   160→    if (!assetPath) return
   161→    transcriptLoaded.current = true
   162→    loadTranscript(audioMeta.asset, assetPath).then(setTranscript)
   163→  }, [data])
   164→
   165→  // ── Preview ↔ Timeline cursor sync ────────────────────────────────────────
   166→
   167→  const onPreviewTimeUpdate = useCallback((time: number) => {
   168→    if (isSyncingFromTimeline.current) return
   169→    isSyncingFromPreview.current = true
   170→    setCurrentTime(time)
   171→    timelineRef.current?.setTime(time)
   172→    requestAnimationFrame(() => {
   173→      isSyncingFromPreview.current = false
   174→    })
   175→  }, [])
   176→
   177→  const onCursorDrag = useCallback((time: number) => {
   178→    if (isSyncingFromPreview.current) return
   179→    isSyncingFromTimeline.current = true
   180→    previewRef.current?.seek(time)
   181→    setCurrentTime(time)
   182→    requestAnimationFrame(() => {
   183→      isSyncingFromTimeline.current = false
   184→    })
   185→  }, [])
   186→
   187→  const onClickTimeArea = useCallback((time: number) => {
   188→    previewRef.current?.seek(time)
   189→    setCurrentTime(time)
   190→    return undefined
   191→  }, [])
   192→
   193→  // ── Timeline editor callbacks (all flow through applyTimelineEdit) ────────
   194→
   195→  // Track start positions before resize begins
   196→  const resizeStartRef = useRef<Record<string, { start: number; end: number; from: number }>>({})
   197→
   198→  const onActionResizeStart = useCallback(({ action }: { action: TimelineAction; row: TimelineRow; dir: string }) => {
   199→    const m = metaRef.current[action.id]
   200→    if (!m) return
   201→    resizeStartRef.current[action.id] = { start: action.start, end: action.end, from: m.from }
   202→  }, [])
   203→
   204→  const onActionResizeEnd = useCallback(({ action, row, dir }: { action: TimelineAction; row: TimelineRow; dir: string; start: number; end: number }) => {
   205→    const m = metaRef.current[action.id]
   206→    const metaUpdates: Record<string, Partial<ClipMeta>> = {}
   207→
   208→    if (dir === 'left') {
   209→      const orig = resizeStartRef.current[action.id]
   210→      if (orig && m) {
   211→        const startDelta = action.start - orig.start
   212→        metaUpdates[action.id] = {
   213→          from: Math.max(0, orig.from + startDelta * m.speed),
   214→        }
   215→      }
   216→    } else if (dir === 'right' && m) {
   217→      metaUpdates[action.id] = {
   218→        to: getSourceTime({ from: m.from, start: action.start, speed: m.speed }, action.end),
   219→      }
   220→    }
   221→
   222→    // Build updated rows with the final action positions
   223→    const newRows = rows.map(r => {
   224→      if (r.id !== row.id) return r
   225→      return {
   226→        ...r,
   227→        actions: r.actions.map(a =>
   228→          a.id === action.id ? { ...a, start: action.start, end: action.end } : a
   229→        ),
   230→      }
   231→    })
   232→
   233→    applyTimelineEdit(newRows, metaUpdates)
   234→    delete resizeStartRef.current[action.id]
   235→  }, [rows, applyTimelineEdit])
   236→
   237→  // Handle data changes from drag/move
   238→  const onChange = useCallback((newRows: TimelineRow[]) => {
   239→    if (ignoreNextOnChange.current) return
   240→    applyTimelineEdit(newRows)
   241→  }, [applyTimelineEdit])
   242→
   243→  // ── Overlay editing ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   244→
   245→  const onOverlayChange = useCallback((actionId: string, patch: Partial<ClipMeta>) => {
   246→    applyTimelineEdit(rows, { [actionId]: patch })
   247→  }, [rows, applyTimelineEdit])
   248→
   249→  // ── Rendering ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   250→
   251→  const getActionRender = useCallback((action: TimelineAction, _row: TimelineRow) => {
   252→    const m = meta[action.id]
   253→    if (!m) return null
   254→    const color = getAssetColor(m.asset)
   255→    const srcEnd = getSourceTime({ from: m.from, start: action.start, speed: m.speed }, action.end)
   256→    return (
   257→      <div
   258→        className="clip-action"
   259→        style={{ backgroundColor: color }}
   260→      >
   261→        <span className="clip-label">{m.asset}</span>
   262→        <span className="clip-time">
   263→          src {m.from.toFixed(1)}s - {srcEnd.toFixed(1)}s
   264→        </span>
   265→      </div>
   266→    )
   267→  }, [meta])
   268→
   269→  // Keyboard: space to toggle play
   270→  useEffect(() => {
   271→    const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
   272→      if (e.code === 'Space' && e.target === document.body) {
   273→        e.preventDefault()
   274→        previewRef.current?.togglePlayPause()
   275→      }
   276→    }
   277→    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)
   278→    return () => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey)
   279→  }, [])
   280→
   281→  const startRender = useCallback(async () => {
   282→    if (renderStatus === 'rendering') return
   283→    setRenderStatus('rendering')
   284→    setRenderLog('')
   285→    try {
   286→      const res = await fetch('/api/render', { method: 'POST' })
   287→      const reader = res.body?.getReader()
   288→      if (!reader) { setRenderStatus('error'); return }
   289→      const decoder = new TextDecoder()
   290→      let buf = ''
   291→      while (true) {
   292→        const { done, value } = await reader.read()
   293→        if (done) break
   294→        buf += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })
   295→        const lines = buf.split('\n')
   296→        buf = lines.pop() ?? ''
   297→        for (const line of lines) {
   298→          if (line.startsWith('event: done')) {
   299→            setRenderStatus('done')
   300→            setRenderDirty(false)
   301→          } else if (line.startsWith('event: error')) {
   302→            setRenderStatus('error')
   303→          } else if (line.startsWith('data: ')) {
   304→            setRenderLog(prev => prev + line.slice(6) + '\n')
   305→          }
   306→        }
   307→      }
   308→    } catch {
   309→      setRenderStatus('error')
   310→    }
   311→  }, [renderStatus])
   312→
   313→  const formatTime = (t: number) => {
   314→    const mins = Math.floor(t / 60)
   315→    const secs = Math.floor(t % 60)
   316→    const ms = Math.floor((t % 1) * 100)
   317→    return `${mins}:${secs.toString().padStart(2, '0')}.${ms.toString().padStart(2, '0')}`
   318→  }
   319→
   320→  const statusIndicator = {
   321→    saved: '●', saving: '◌', dirty: '○', error: '✕',
   322→  }[saveStatus]
   323→
   324→  const statusColor = {
   325→    saved: '#98c379', saving: '#e5c07b', dirty: '#e5c07b', error: '#e06c75',
   326→  }[saveStatus]
   327→
   328→  if (!data) {
   329→    return <div className="app" style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center' }}>Loading timeline...</div>
   330→  }
   331→
   332→  return (
   333→    <div className="app">
   334→      <div className="top-bar">
   335→        <h1>Timeline Viewer</h1>
   336→        <div className="top-bar-right">
   337→          <button
   338→            className={`render-btn${renderDirty ? ' render-dirty' : ''}${renderStatus === 'rendering' ? ' rendering' : ''}`}
   339→            onClick={startRender}
   340→            disabled={renderStatus === 'rendering'}
   341→            title={renderLog || undefined}
   342→          >
   343→            {renderStatus === 'rendering' ? 'Rendering...' : renderDirty ? 'Render' : 'Render'}
   344→          </button>
   345→          <span className="save-status" style={{ color: statusColor }}>
   346→            {statusIndicator} {saveStatus}
   347→          </span>
   348→          <span className="timecode">{formatTime(currentTime)}</span>
   349→        </div>
   350→      </div>
   351→
   352→      <div className="video-container">
   353→        <LivePreview
   354→          ref={previewRef}
   355→          rows={rows}
   356→          meta={meta}
   357→          assetPaths={data.assetMap}
   358→          transcript={transcript}
   359→          background={data.header.output.background ? data.assetMap[data.header.output.background] : undefined}
   360→          backgroundScale={data.header.output.background_scale}
   361→          onTimeUpdate={onPreviewTimeUpdate}
   362→        />
   363→        <OverlayEditor
   364→          rows={rows}
   365→          meta={meta}
   366→          currentTime={currentTime}
   367→          canvasRef={canvasRef}
   368→          backgroundScale={data.header.output.background_scale ?? 1}
   369→          onOverlayChange={onOverlayChange}
   370→        />
   371→      </div>
   372→
   373→      <div className="timeline-container">
   374→        <div className="track-labels">
   375→          {rows.map((row) => (
   376→            <div key={row.id} className="track-label">
   377→              {getRowLabel(row.id, meta, rows)}
   378→            </div>
   379→          ))}
   380→        </div>
   381→        <div className="timeline-wrapper">
   382→          <Timeline
   383→            ref={timelineRef}
   384→            style={{ width: '100%', height: '100%' }}
   385→            editorData={rows}
   386→            effects={data.effects}
   387→            onChange={onChange}
   388→            scale={5}
   389→            scaleWidth={160}
   390→            scaleSplitCount={5}
   391→            startLeft={20}
   392→            rowHeight={40}
   393→            autoScroll={true}
   394→            dragLine={true}
   395→            getActionRender={getActionRender}
   396→            onCursorDrag={onCursorDrag}
   397→            onClickTimeArea={onClickTimeArea}
   398→            onActionResizeStart={onActionResizeStart}
   399→            onActionResizeEnd={onActionResizeEnd}
   400→          />
   401→        </div>
   402→      </div>
   403→    </div>
   404→  )
   405→}
   406→
   407→export default App
   408→

   189→    setCurrentTime(time)
   190→    return undefined
   191→  }, [])
   192→
   193→  // ── Timeline editor callbacks (all flow through applyTimelineEdit) ────────
   194→
   195→  // Track start positions before resize begins
   196→  const resizeStartRef = useRef<Record<string, { start: number; end: number; from: number }>>({})
   197→
   198→  const onActionResizeStart = useCallback(({ action }: { action: TimelineAction; row: TimelineRow; dir: string }) => {
   199→    const m = metaRef.current[action.id]
   200→    if (!m) return
   201→    resizeStartRef.current[action.id] = { start: action.start, end: action.end, from: m.from }
   202→  }, [])
   203→
   204→  const onActionResizeEnd = useCallback(({ action, row, dir }: { action: TimelineAction; row: TimelineRow; dir: string; start: number; end: number }) => {
   205→    const m = metaRef.current[action.id]
   206→    const metaUpdates: Record<string, Partial<ClipMeta>> = {}
   207→
   208→    if (dir === 'left') {
   209→      const orig = resizeStartRef.current[action.id]
   210→      if (orig && m) {
   211→        const startDelta = action.start - orig.start
   212→        metaUpdates[action.id] = {
   213→          from: Math.max(0, orig.from + startDelta * m.speed),
   214→        }
   215→      }
   216→    } else if (dir === 'right' && m) {
   217→      metaUpdates[action.id] = {
   218→        to: getSourceTime({ from: m.from, start: action.start, speed: m.speed }, action.end),
   219→      }
   220→    }
   221→
   222→    // Build updated rows with the final action positions
   223→    const newRows = rows.map(r => {
   224→      if (r.id !== row.id) return r
   225→      return {
   226→        ...r,
   227→        actions: r.actions.map(a =>
   228→          a.id === action.id ? { ...a, start: action.start, end: action.end } : a
   229→        ),
   230→      }
   231→    })
   232→
   233→    applyTimelineEdit(newRows, metaUpdates)
   234→    delete resizeStartRef.current[action.id]
   235→  }, [rows, applyTimelineEdit])
   236→
   237→  // Handle data changes from drag/move
   238→  const onChange = useCallback((newRows: TimelineRow[]) => {
   239→    if (ignoreNextOnChange.current) return
   240→    applyTimelineEdit(newRows)
   241→  }, [applyTimelineEdit])
   242→
   243→  // ── Overlay editing ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   244→
   245→  const onOverlayChange = useCallback((actionId: string, patch: Partial<ClipMeta>) => {
   246→    applyTimelineEdit(rows, { [actionId]: patch })
   247→  }, [rows, applyTimelineEdit])
   248→
   249→  // ── Rendering ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   250→
   251→  const getActionRender = useCallback((action: TimelineAction, _row: TimelineRow) => {
   252→    const m = meta[action.id]
   253→    if (!m) return null
   254→    const color = getAssetColor(m.asset)
   255→    const srcEnd = getSourceTime({ from: m.from, start: action.start, speed: m.speed }, action.end)
   256→    return (
   257→      <div
   258→        className="clip-action"
   259→        style={{ backgroundColor: color }}
   260→      >
   261→        <span className="clip-label">{m.asset}</span>
   262→        <span className="clip-time">
   263→          src {m.from.toFixed(1)}s - {srcEnd.toFixed(1)}s
   264→        </span>
   265→      </div>
   266→    )
   267→  }, [meta])
   268→
   269→  // Keyboard: space to toggle play
   270→  useEffect(() => {
   271→    const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
   272→      if (e.code === 'Space' && e.target === document.body) {
   273→        e.preventDefault()
   274→        previewRef.current?.togglePlayPause()
   275→      }
   276→    }
   277→    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)
   278→    return () => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey)
   279→  }, [])
   280→
   281→  const startRender = useCallback(async () => {
   282→    if (renderStatus === 'rendering') return
   283→    setRenderStatus('rendering')
   284→    setRenderLog('')
   285→    try {
   286→      const res = await fetch('/api/render', { method: 'POST' })
   287→      const reader = res.body?.getReader()
   288→      if (!reader) { setRenderStatus('error'); return }
   289→      const decoder = new TextDecoder()
   290→      let buf = ''
   291→      while (true) {
   292→        const { done, value } = await reader.read()
   293→        if (done) break
   294→        buf += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })
   295→        const lines = buf.split('\n')
   296→        buf = lines.pop() ?? ''
   297→        for (const line of lines) {
   298→          if (line.startsWith('event: done')) {
   299→            setRenderStatus('done')
   300→            setRenderDirty(false)
   301→          } else if (line.startsWith('event: error')) {
   302→            setRenderStatus('error')
   303→          } else if (line.startsWith('data: ')) {
   304→            setRenderLog(prev => prev + line.slice(6) + '\n')
   305→          }
   306→        }
   307→      }
   308→    } catch {
   309→      setRenderStatus('error')
   310→    }
   311→  }, [renderStatus])
   312→
   313→  const formatTime = (t: number) => {
   314→    const mins = Math.floor(t / 60)
   315→    const secs = Math.floor(t % 60)
   316→    const ms = Math.floor((t % 1) * 100)
   317→    return `${mins}:${secs.toString().padStart(2, '0')}.${ms.toString().padStart(2, '0')}`
   318→  }
   319→
   320→  const statusIndicator = {
   321→    saved: '●', saving: '◌', dirty: '○', error: '✕',
   322→  }[saveStatus]
   323→
   324→  const statusColor = {
   325→    saved: '#98c379', saving: '#e5c07b', dirty: '#e5c07b', error: '#e06c75',
   326→  }[saveStatus]
   327→
   328→  if (!data) {
   329→    return <div className="app" style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center' }}>Loading timeline...</div>
   330→  }
   331→
   332→  return (
   333→    <div className="app">
   334→      <div className="top-bar">
   335→        <h1>Timeline Viewer</h1>
   336→        <div className="top-bar-right">
   337→          <button
   338→            className={`render-btn${renderDirty ? ' render-dirty' : ''}${renderStatus === 'rendering' ? ' rendering' : ''}`}
   339→            onClick={startRender}
   340→            disabled={renderStatus === 'rendering'}
   341→            title={renderLog || undefined}
   342→          >
   343→            {renderStatus === 'rendering' ? 'Rendering...' : renderDirty ? 'Render' : 'Render'}
   344→          </button>
   345→          <span className="save-status" style={{ color: statusColor }}>
   346→            {statusIndicator} {saveStatus}
   347→          </span>
   348→          <span className="timecode">{formatTime(currentTime)}</span>
   349→        </div>
   350→      </div>
   351→
   352→      <div className="video-container">
   353→        <LivePreview
   354→          ref={previewRef}
   355→          rows={rows}
   356→          meta={meta}
   357→          assetPaths={data.assetMap}
   358→          transcript={transcript}
   359→          background={data.header.output.background ? data.assetMap[data.header.output.background] : undefined}
   360→          backgroundScale={data.header.output.background_scale}
   361→          onTimeUpdate={onPreviewTimeUpdate}
   362→        />
   363→        <OverlayEditor
   364→          rows={rows}
   365→          meta={meta}
   366→          currentTime={currentTime}
   367→          canvasRef={canvasRef}
   368→          backgroundScale={data.header.output.background_scale ?? 1}
   369→          onOverlayChange={onOverlayChange}
   370→        />
   371→      </div>
   372→
   373→      <div className="timeline-container">
   374→        <div className="track-labels">
   375→          {rows.map((row) => (
   376→            <div key={row.id} className="track-label">
   377→              {getRowLabel(row.id, meta, rows)}
   378→            </div>
   379→          ))}
   380→        </div>
   381→        <div className="timeline-wrapper">
   382→          <Timeline
   383→            ref={timelineRef}
   384→            style={{ width: '100%', height: '100%' }}
   385→            editorData={rows}
   386→            effects={data.effects}
   387→            onChange={onChange}
   388→            scale={5}
   389→            scaleWidth={160}
   390→            scaleSplitCount={5}
   391→            startLeft={20}
   392→            rowHeight={40}
   393→            autoScroll={true}
   394→            dragLine={true}
   395→            getActionRender={getActionRender}
   396→            onCursorDrag={onCursorDrag}
   397→            onClickTimeArea={onClickTimeArea}
   398→            onActionResizeStart={onActionResizeStart}
   399→            onActionResizeEnd={onActionResizeEnd}
   400→          />
   401→        </div>
   402→      </div>
   403→    </div>
   404→  )
   405→}
   406→
   407→export default App
   408→

    51→
    52→export function getAssetColor(asset: string): string {
    53→  return ASSET_COLORS[asset] ?? '#abb2bf'
    54→}
    55→
    56→// Compute source media time from timeline time
    57→export function getSourceTime(clip: { from: number; start: number; speed: number }, time: number): number {
    58→  return clip.from + (time - clip.start) * clip.speed
    59→}
    60→
    61→export interface TranscriptSegment {
    62→  start: number  // source audio time
    63→  end: number
    64→  text: string
    65→}

    67→export interface TimelineData {
    68→  rows: TimelineRow[]
    69→  meta: Record<string, ClipMeta>
    70→  effects: Record<string, TimelineEffect>
    71→  assetMap: Record<string, string>
    72→  header: { output: RawTimeline['output']; asset_map: RawTimeline['asset_map'] }

    74→
    75→// Load transcript segments from asset profile
    76→export async function loadTranscript(assetKey: string, assetPath: string): Promise<TranscriptSegment[]> {
    77→  const filename = assetPath.split('/').pop() ?? ''
    78→  const ext = filename.includes('.') ? filename.slice(filename.lastIndexOf('.')) : ''
    79→
    80→  // Try filename first, then asset key + extension
    81→  for (const name of [filename, `${assetKey}${ext}`]) {
    82→    const res = await fetch(`/media/asset_profiles/${name}.yaml`)
    83→    if (!res.ok) continue
    84→    const text = await res.text()
    85→    const profile = yaml.load(text) as { transcript?: { segments?: TranscriptSegment[] } }
    86→    const segments = profile?.transcript?.segments
    87→    if (segments?.length) return segments
    88→  }
    89→  return []
    90→}
    91→
    92→function buildFromRaw(timeline: RawTimeline): TimelineData {
    93→  const effects: Record<string, TimelineEffect> = {}
    94→  for (const clip of timeline.clips) {
    95→    const effectId = `effect-${clip.asset}`
    96→    if (!effects[effectId]) {
    97→      effects[effectId] = { id: effectId }
    98→    }
    99→  }
   100→
   101→  const videoActions: TimelineAction[] = []
   102→  const audioRowMap: Record<string, TimelineAction[]> = {}
   103→  const overlayActions: TimelineAction[] = []
   104→  const meta: Record<string, ClipMeta> = {}
   105→
   106→  // Track audio row assignment: each unique asset gets its own row
   107→  let audioRowCounter = 0
   108→  const assetToAudioRow: Record<string, string> = {}
   109→
   110→  for (const [i, clip] of timeline.clips.entries()) {
   111→    const speed = clip.speed ?? 1
   112→    let duration: number
   113→    if (clip.track === 'overlay' && clip.hold != null) {
   114→      duration = clip.hold
   115→    } else {
   116→      duration = (clip.to - clip.from) / speed
   117→    }
   118→    const action: TimelineAction = {
   119→      id: `clip-${i}`,
   120→      start: clip.at,
   121→      end: clip.at + duration,
   122→      effectId: `effect-${clip.asset}`,
   123→    }
   124→    meta[action.id] = {
   125→      asset: clip.asset,
   126→      track: clip.track,
   127→      from: clip.from ?? 0,
   128→      to: clip.to ?? (clip.hold ?? 0),
   129→      speed,
   130→      volume: clip.volume ?? 1.0,
   131→      x: clip.x ?? 0,
   132→      y: clip.y ?? 0,
   133→      width: clip.width ?? 320,
   134→      height: clip.height ?? 240,
   135→      opacity: clip.opacity ?? 1.0,
   136→    }
   137→    if (clip.track === 'video') {
   138→      videoActions.push(action)
   139→    } else if (clip.track === 'overlay') {
   140→      overlayActions.push(action)
   141→    } else {
   142→      // Assign each audio asset to its own row for multi-track support
   143→      if (!assetToAudioRow[clip.asset]) {
   144→        assetToAudioRow[clip.asset] = `row-audio-${audioRowCounter++}`
   145→      }
   146→      const rowId = assetToAudioRow[clip.asset]
   147→      if (!audioRowMap[rowId]) audioRowMap[rowId] = []
   148→      audioRowMap[rowId].push(action)
   149→    }
   150→  }
   151→
   152→  const audioRows: TimelineRow[] = Object.entries(audioRowMap).map(
   153→    ([id, actions]) => ({ id, actions })
   154→  )
   155→
   156→  return {
   157→    rows: [
   158→      { id: 'row-video', actions: videoActions },
   159→      ...audioRows,
   160→      { id: 'row-overlay', actions: overlayActions },
   161→    ],
   162→    meta,
   163→    effects,
   164→    assetMap: timeline.asset_map,
   165→    header: { output: timeline.output, asset_map: timeline.asset_map },
   166→  }
   167→}
   168→
   169→// Parse yaml text into timeline data
   170→export function parseTimeline(text: string): TimelineData {
   171→  const timeline = yaml.load(text) as RawTimeline
   172→  return buildFromRaw(timeline)
   173→}
   174→
   175→// Convert editor state back to YAML string
   176→export function toYaml(
   177→  rows: TimelineRow[],
   178→  meta: Record<string, ClipMeta>,
   179→  header: TimelineData['header'],
   180→): string {
   181→  const clips: RawClip[] = []
   182→
   183→  function rowTrack(rowId: string): 'video' | 'audio' | 'overlay' | null {
   184→    if (rowId === 'row-video') return 'video'
   185→    if (rowId.startsWith('row-audio')) return 'audio'
   186→    if (rowId === 'row-overlay') return 'overlay'
   187→    return null
   188→  }
   189→
   190→  for (const row of rows) {
   191→    const track = rowTrack(row.id)
   192→    if (!track) continue
   193→    const sorted = [...row.actions].sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start)
   194→    for (const action of sorted) {
   195→      const m = meta[action.id]
   196→      if (!m) continue
   197→
   198→      if (track === 'overlay') {
   199→        const clip: RawClip = {
   200→          at: round(action.start),
   201→          track,
   202→          asset: m.asset,
   203→          from: 0,
   204→          to: 0,
   205→          hold: round(action.end - action.start),
   206→          x: round(m.x),
   207→          y: round(m.y),
   208→          width: round(m.width),
   209→          height: round(m.height),
   210→          opacity: round(m.opacity),
   211→        }
   212→        clips.push(clip)
   213→      } else {
   214→        const clip: RawClip = {
   215→          at: round(action.start),
   216→          track,
   217→          asset: m.asset,
   218→          from: round(m.from),
   219→          to: round(getSourceTime({ from: m.from, start: action.start, speed: m.speed }, action.end)),
   220→        }
   221→        if (m.speed !== 1) {
   222→          clip.speed = round(m.speed)
   223→        }
   224→        if (track === 'audio' && m.volume !== 1) {
   225→          clip.volume = round(m.volume)
   226→        }
   227→        clips.push(clip)
   228→      }
   229→    }
   230→  }
   231→
   232→  const doc = {
   233→    output: header.output,
   234→    asset_map: header.asset_map,
   235→    clips,
   236→  }
   237→
   238→  return yaml.dump(doc, {
   239→    lineWidth: -1,
   240→    noRefs: true,
   241→    quotingType: '"',
   242→    forceQuotes: false,
   243→  })
   244→}
   245→
   246→function round(n: number): number {
   247→  return Math.round(n * 100) / 100
   248→}

   455→          vid.play()
   456→        }
   457→        drawVideoFrame(vid)
   458→        finishFrameRef.current(time)

   461→        vid.pause()
   462→        vid.currentTime = sourceTime
   463→        activeVideoClip.current = clip.actionId

   465→      }
   466→    },
   467→    [findClipAt, clips, drawVideoFrame, drawTranscript, drawWhenReady],
   468→  )
   469→
   470→  // Refs so the RAF loop always sees the latest sync functions.
   471→  const syncVideoRef = useRef(syncVideo)
   472→  const syncAudioRef = useRef(syncAudio)
   473→  const onTimeUpdateRef = useRef(onTimeUpdate)
   474→  const finishFrameRef = useRef(finishFrame)
   475→  syncVideoRef.current = syncVideo
   476→  syncAudioRef.current = syncAudio
   477→  onTimeUpdateRef.current = onTimeUpdate
   478→  finishFrameRef.current = finishFrame
   479→
   480→  // RAF playback loop
   481→  const tick = useCallback(() => {
   482→    if (!playing.current) return
   483→
   484→    const elapsed = (performance.now() - startWall.current) / 1000
   485→    const time = startTimeline.current + elapsed
   486→    currentTime.current = time
   487→
   488→    syncVideoRef.current(time, true)
   489→    syncAudioRef.current(time, true)
   490→    onTimeUpdateRef.current(time)
   491→
   492→    rafId.current = requestAnimationFrame(tick)
   493→  }, [])
   494→
   495→  const seek = useCallback(
   496→    (time: number) => {
   497→      currentTime.current = time
   498→      if (playing.current) {
   499→        startWall.current = performance.now()
   500→        startTimeline.current = time
   501→      }
   502→      syncVideo(time, playing.current)
   503→      syncAudio(time, playing.current)
   504→      onTimeUpdate(time)
   505→    },
   506→    [syncVideo, syncAudio, onTimeUpdate],
   507→  )
   508→
   509→  const play = useCallback(() => {
   510→    if (playing.current) return
   511→    playing.current = true
   512→    setIsPlaying(true)
   513→    startWall.current = performance.now()
   514→    startTimeline.current = currentTime.current
   515→    rafId.current = requestAnimationFrame(tick)
   516→  }, [tick])
   517→
   518→  const pause = useCallback(() => {
   519→    if (!playing.current) return
   520→    playing.current = false
   521→    setIsPlaying(false)
   522→    cancelAnimationFrame(rafId.current)
   523→    for (const vid of Object.values(videoElements.current)) {
   524→      vid.pause()
   525→    }
   526→    for (const aud of Object.values(audioElements.current)) {
   527→      aud.pause()
   528→    }
   529→    activeVideoClip.current = null
   530→    activeAudioClips.current = new Set()
   531→    syncVideo(currentTime.current, false)
   532→  }, [syncVideo])
   533→
   534→  const togglePlayPause = useCallback(() => {
   535→    if (playing.current) {
   536→      pause()
   537→    } else {
   538→      play()
   539→    }
   540→  }, [play, pause])
   541→
   542→  // Force re-sync using refs (always has latest data, no stale closures)
   543→  const refresh = useCallback(() => {
   544→    activeVideoClip.current = null
   545→    activeAudioClips.current = new Set()
   546→    const t = currentTime.current
   547→    if (playing.current) {
   548→      startWall.current = performance.now()
   549→      startTimeline.current = t
   550→    }
   551→    syncVideoRef.current(t, playing.current)
   552→    syncAudioRef.current(t, playing.current)
   553→  }, [])
   554→
   555→  useImperativeHandle(
   556→    ref,
   557→    () => ({
   558→      seek,
   559→      play,
   560→      pause,
   561→      togglePlayPause,
   562→      refresh,
   563→      get isPlaying() {
   564→        return playing.current
   565→      },
   566→      get canvasElement() {
   567→        return canvasRef.current
   568→      },
   569→    }),
   570→    [seek, play, pause, togglePlayPause, refresh],
   571→  )
   572→
   573→  // When clips change while paused, re-draw so the preview reflects
   574→  // the new positions. (During playback, the RAF loop handles this
   575→  // automatically via syncVideoRef/syncAudioRef.)
   576→  useEffect(() => {
   577→    if (!playing.current) {
   578→      activeVideoClip.current = null
   579→      activeAudioClips.current = new Set()
   580→      syncVideo(currentTime.current, false)
   581→      syncAudio(currentTime.current, false)
   582→    }
   583→  }, [clips, syncVideo, syncAudio])
   584→
   585→  // Draw initial black frame
   586→  useEffect(() => {
   587→    drawBlack()
   588→    compositeToCanvas()
   589→  }, [drawBlack, compositeToCanvas])
   590→
   591→  return (
   592→    <div className="live-preview">
   593→      <canvas
   594→        ref={canvasRef}
   595→        width={1280}
   596→        height={720}
   597→        className="preview-canvas"
   598→      />
   599→      <button className="skip-btn" onClick={() => seek(0)} title="Jump to beginning">
   600→        ⏮
   601→      </button>
   602→      <button className="play-btn" onClick={togglePlayPause}>
   603→        {isPlaying ? '⏸' : '▶'}
   604→      </button>
   605→    </div>
   606→  )
   607→})
   608→
   609→export default LivePreview

Perfect! I've read all three files. Let me provide you with a comprehensive summary of the timeline data model and asset flow:

## Asset Map (Complete)

The `asset_map` in `timeline.yaml` defines all available assets:

```yaml
bg-dark-abstract: inputs/bg-dark-abstract.png
demo-one: inputs/demo-one.mp4
demo-two: inputs/demo-two.mp4
example-video: inputs/example-video.mp4
example-image1: inputs/example-image1.jpg
example-image2: inputs/example-image2.jpg
input: inputs/audio.MP3
output-composition: inputs/output_composition.webm
venn-diagram: inputs/venn_diagram_video.webm
```

This maps logical asset names (e.g., `demo-one`) to actual file paths (e.g., `inputs/demo-one.mp4`).

## How Assets Are Added to Timeline (YAML Actions)

Assets are added via **clips** array in the YAML. Each clip references an asset and specifies:
- `asset`: The key from `asset_map`
- `track`: Which track it goes on (`video`, `audio`, or `overlay`)
- `at`: Start time on timeline (seconds)
- `from`: Source media start time (seconds)
- `to`: Source media end time (seconds)
- Optional: `speed`, `volume`, `hold` (for overlays), `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `opacity`

Example from the timeline:
```yaml
- at: 0
  track: video
  asset: output-composition
  from: 0
  to: 6.91
```

## Track Structure

Three tracks exist:
1. **video** (`row-video`): Single track for video clips
2. **audio** (`row-audio-*`): Multiple rows (one per unique audio asset) for multi-track support
3. **overlay** (`row-overlay`): Single track for image/text overlays

In the current timeline:
- Video track: 4 clips (output-composition, venn-diagram, demo-one, demo-two)
- Audio track: 1 clip (input audio)
- Overlay track: Currently empty

## How Viewer Loads Assets (assetPaths Mechanism)

In `App.tsx`:
1. The parsed `TimelineData` contains `assetMap` (same as YAML's `asset_map`)
2. This is passed to `LivePreview` as `assetPaths` prop (line 357)
3. `LivePreview` uses these paths to fetch media files from the server
4. The server serves files from the working directory (relative paths like `inputs/demo-one.mp4`)

Timeline-data.ts also loads transcript metadata for audio assets via `loadTranscript()`, checking for YAML profile files in `/media/asset_profiles/`.

## UI for Browsing/Adding Assets

**Currently: NO UI exists for asset management.**

The current UI provides:
- Timeline editor (drag, resize clips)
- Live preview of video
- Overlay position editor (OverlayEditor component)
- Playback controls (space to play/pause)
- Save status indicator
- Render button (launches backend render)

**What's missing:**
- No asset browser/picker
- No way to add new assets to the asset_map via UI
- No way to add new clips via UI (must edit YAML directly)
- Assets must be manually added to `timeline.yaml`

The workflow currently requires:
1. Place media files in the `inputs/` directory
2. Manually add entries to the `asset_map` in `timeline.yaml`
3. Manually add clips to the `clips` array
4. UI polls for changes and reflects them (line 134-150 in App.tsx)

---

**Key architectural insight:** The system has a clean separation between data (YAML) and UI (React viewer). The UI is read-only for assets—it only displays and edits timing/positioning. To manage the asset library, you'd need to build UI components that can modify the `asset_map` and create/edit clips programmatically, then save back to YAML.

## Summary of the Viewer Application

### 1. Component Hierarchy in src/

The application has a simple, flat component structure:

- **App.tsx** - Root component, main state management, timeline editor integration
- **LivePreview.tsx** - Canvas-based video/audio preview renderer with playback controls
- **OverlayEditor.tsx** - Interactive overlay positioning and resizing editor
- **timeline-data.ts** - Data parsing and utility functions (not a component)
- **main.tsx** - React entry point
- **App.css** - All styling (dark NLE theme)
- **index.css** - Minimal reset styles

No subdirectory structure—everything is flat in src/.

### 2. Current Timeline Display in App.tsx

The timeline is displayed in a **three-part layout**:

**Top Bar (lines 334-350):**
- Title: "Timeline Viewer"
- Right side: Render button (with dirty/rendering states), save status indicator (●◌○✕), timecode display

**Video Container (lines 352-371):**
- **LivePreview**: Canvas-based preview (1280x720, dark background)
- **OverlayEditor**: Overlaid interactive editor for positioning overlays
- Both centered in the middle section

**Timeline Container (lines 373-402):**
- **Track Labels** (left sidebar, 80px wide):
  - Uses `getRowLabel()` function to display: "Video", "Audio" (per track), "Overlay"
  - Gets label for audio rows from first action's asset metadata
  - Height: 160px fixed
  
- **Timeline Wrapper** (scrollable right side):
  - Uses `@xzdarcy/react-timeline-editor` library
  - Configuration:
    - scale: 5 (time units per pixel)
    - scaleWidth: 160
    - rowHeight: 40
    - Auto-scroll enabled
    - Drag line cursor
  - Clips rendered with `getActionRender()` showing:
    - Asset name
    - Source time range (e.g., "src 0.0s - 6.9s")
    - Color-coded by asset

### 3. Timeline Data Model (timeline-data.ts)

**Key Interfaces:**

```typescript
interface ClipMeta {
  asset: string                          // asset key
  track: 'video' | 'audio' | 'overlay'
  from: number                           // start time in source media (seconds)
  to: number                             // end time in source media
  speed: number                          // playback speed multiplier
  volume: number                         // audio volume (0-1)
  x, y, width, height: number            // overlay positioning
  opacity: number                        // overlay opacity
}

interface RawClip {
  at: number                             // timeline start position
  track: 'video' | 'audio' | 'overlay'
  asset: string                          // asset key
  from: number                           // source start
  to: number                             // source end
  speed?: number                         // optional, defaults to 1
  volume?: number                        // optional, defaults to 1.0
  hold?: number                          // overlay duration (instead of to-from)
  x?, y?, width?, height?, opacity?      // optional overlay properties
}

interface RawTimeline {
  output: { resolution, fps, file, background?, background_scale? }
  asset_map: Record<string, string>      // maps asset keys to file paths
  clips: RawClip[]
}

interface TimelineData {
  rows: TimelineRow[]                    // react-timeline-editor format
  meta: Record<string, ClipMeta>         // clip-id -> metadata
  effects: Record<string, TimelineEffect>
  assetMap: Record<string, string>
  header: { output, asset_map }
}
```

**Row Creation (buildFromRaw, lines 92-167):**

1. Creates effect per unique asset
2. Processes clips and groups by track:
   - **Video track**: Single row (`row-video`), all video clips
   - **Audio tracks**: One row per unique audio asset (`row-audio-0`, `row-audio-1`, etc.)
   - **Overlay track**: Single row (`row-overlay`), all overlay clips
3. Calculates duration from `to - from / speed` (or `hold` for overlays)
4. Stores metadata indexed by clip ID (`clip-0`, `clip-1`, etc.)

### 4. Asset Map (timeline.yaml)

The `asset_map` section maps **asset keys** to **file paths**:

```yaml
asset_map:
  bg-dark-abstract: inputs/bg-dark-abstract.png
  demo-one: inputs/demo-one.mp4
  example-video: inputs/example-video.mp4
  input: inputs/audio.MP3
  venn-diagram: inputs/venn_diagram_video.webm
  output-composition: inputs/output_composition.webm
  # ... etc
```

Used by:
- LivePreview to load media at `/media/{path}`
- OverlayEditor for overlay positioning
- Asset color mapping (ASSET_COLORS record in timeline-data.ts)

### 5. Existing Asset Browser/Panel Functionality

**There is NO asset browser or panel currently implemented.** The UI shows:
- Only what's already on the timeline
- No asset library view
- No drag-drop to add assets
- No asset properties panel

### 6. Current Layout

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Timeline Viewer        [Render] ● saved    0:00.00  │  <- Top bar
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                      │
│                    [CANVAS 1280x720]                 │  <- Video Container

│                                                      │
├──────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┤

**Specific Dimensions:**
- Canvas: 1280x720
- Timeline height: 160px fixed
- Track labels: 80px wide
- Row height: 40px each
- Top bar: ~48px

**Color Scheme (CSS variables):**
- Primary bg: `#1e1e2e` (dark)
- Secondary bg: `#181825` (darker)
- Surface: `#313244` (lighter surfaces)
- Text primary: `#cdd6f4`
- Accent: `#89b4fa` (blue)

### 7. Key Features & Capabilities

**Editing:**
- Drag clips left/right on timeline
- Resize clips (left/right edges)
- Resize overlays with corner handles
- Move overlays on canvas
- Changes auto-save to YAML (500ms debounce)

**Playback:**
- Canvas-based live preview with video, audio, overlay composition
- Timeline cursor syncs with preview
- Space bar to play/pause
- Skip to beginning button

**Data Flow:**
1. YAML loaded via `/api/timeline` (polled every 1s)
2. Parsed into TimelineData
3. Rows/meta displayed in timeline editor
4. Edits scheduled for save
5. Save POST to `/api/save-timeline`
6. Render triggered via `/api/render` (SSE for logs)
